items.exampleCN: 中世纪天使学将天使分为九个等级。

definition_zh: 盈利能力；获利性；利润水平
definition_en: the ability of a business or activity to produce a profit, or the measured degree of that ability
core_image: 几张报表并排摊开，每张都用一条斜线标出「每一元钱能带回多少」
scene: 董事会把几张报表并排摊开，逐行比较每一条业务线能带回多少。 Analysts questioned the profitability of the new plant.
sceneCN: 董事们并排比对报表，逐条业务线核算回报；句中的 profitability 指「一项业务产生利润的能力」（第 1 个义项：企业或业务持续获利的能力）。图中可辨识物件：并排的报表、折线、比例尺、钢笔、咖啡杯。

pos.zh: 盈利能力；获利性；利润水平

forms.label: 复数（罕用，指多种获利水平）

senses.title: The ability to produce profit
senses.definition: the capacity of a business, product or activity to produce a profit rather than a loss
senses.definitionCN: 企业、产品或活动产生利润而非亏损的能力
senses.example: Analysts questioned the profitability of the new plant.
senses.exampleCN: 分析师质疑新工厂的盈利能力。
senses.why: The suffix turns the adjective into a quality, so the noun names the capacity that a profitable thing has.
senses.whyCN: 后缀把形容词变成一种性质，因此这个名词指「有利可图之物」所具备的能力。

senses.title: The measured degree of gain
senses.definition: the extent to which an operation earns more than it costs, expressed as a figure or a level
senses.definitionCN: 一项经营赚得超过成本的程度，以数字或水平表示
senses.example: Profitability fell from one quarter to the next.
senses.exampleCN: 盈利能力从一个季度到下一个季度下降。
senses.why: A quality that can rise and fall must be measurable, and the noun is used for the measurement itself.
senses.whyCN: 一种能升能降的性质必然可计量，这个名词就用于指那个计量结果。

senses.title: A financial ratio or indicator
senses.definition: one of the standard ratios, such as return on sales or on capital, used to express gain
senses.definitionCN: 用来表示获利的标准比率之一，如销售回报率或资本回报率
senses.example: The report lists three measures of profitability.
senses.exampleCN: 报告列出三项盈利能力指标。
senses.why: Accounting prefers ratios because they compare firms of different size, so the abstract noun becomes a family of indicators.
senses.whyCN: 会计偏好比率，因为比率能比较规模不同的企业，于是这个抽象名词变成一组指标。

senses.title: A management goal
senses.definition: a target that managers pursue when they try to raise the surplus earned on each sale
senses.definitionCN: 管理者为提高每笔销售所赚盈余而追求的目标
senses.example: Improving profitability became the board's first priority.
senses.exampleCN: 提高盈利能力成为董事会的首要任务。
senses.why: Once measured, a quality can be aimed at, and the noun moves from description to objective.
senses.whyCN: 一旦可计量，一种性质就能成为瞄准的对象，这个名词便从描述转为目标。

senses.title: The level across a sector
senses.definition: the average ability of firms in an industry or region to earn a surplus
senses.definitionCN: 某一行业或地区的企业平均赚取盈余的能力
senses.example: Sector-wide profitability has fallen since the price cap.
senses.exampleCN: 自价格上限实施以来，整个行业的盈利能力下降。
senses.why: Comparisons are usually made between groups, so the noun is applied to aggregates rather than single firms.
senses.whyCN: 比较通常在群体之间进行，因此这个名词被用于加总体，而不是单个企业。

senses.title: Sustained gain over the long run
senses.definition: the ability to keep earning a surplus across many years and through downturns
senses.definitionCN: 在多年间、穿越衰退仍持续赚取盈余的能力
senses.example: Long-term profitability matters more to pension funds than a single strong year.
senses.exampleCN: 对养老基金而言，长期盈利能力比单独一个丰收年更重要。
senses.why: Investors with long horizons care about durability, so the noun acquires a time dimension.
senses.whyCN: 长期投资者看重持久性，这个名词因此带上时间维度。

senses.title: The gain of a specific product line
senses.titleCN: 某一产品线的获利情况
senses.definition: the surplus earned by one product, service or branch compared with the rest
senses.definitionCN: 某一产品、服务或分支相较于其余部分所赚的盈余
senses.example: They discontinued the line despite its early profitability.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管这条产品线早期获利，他们还是把它停掉了。
senses.why: Firms need to know which part pays for the others, so the noun is attached to individual units.
senses.whyCN: 企业需要知道哪一部分在养活其余部分，因此这个名词被挂到具体单元上。

senses.title: The quality of yielding more than cost
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：收益高于代价的性质
senses.definition: the general quality of any arrangement that returns more than it consumes
senses.definitionCN: 任何安排所具有的「回报多于消耗」的一般性质
senses.example: The charity judged the profitability of the scheme in hours saved, not money.
senses.exampleCN: 该慈善机构以节省的工时而非金钱来衡量这项方案的收益。
senses.why: Stripped of ledgers, the noun still compares return with cost, whatever units are used on either side.
senses.whyCN: 剥去账本之后，这个名词仍在比较回报与代价，无论两边用的是什么单位。

intro.en: Profitability is profitable plus the Latin-derived suffix -ity, which turns an adjective into a noun of quality. The word belongs to modern commercial and statistical writing. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: profitability 由 profitable 加源自拉丁语、把形容词转为性质名词的后缀构成。这个词属于近代商业与统计写作。年代为约数。

items.en: The noun profit goes back to profectus 'advance, gain', from proficere 'to make progress'.
items.cn: 名词 profit 可追溯到 profectus「前进、增益」，来自 proficere「取得进展」。

items.en: Profitable, formed with the suffix of capacity, is recorded in the late fourteenth century.
items.cn: profitable 由表示「能力」的后缀构成，在十四世纪晚期已有记录。

items.en: The suffix -ity continues Latin -itas, which names a state or quality and reached English through French forms.
items.cn: 表示性质的后缀承自拉丁语 -itas，用来指状态或性质，并经法语形式进入英语。

items.en: Profitability appears in nineteenth-century commercial writing, when firms began to compare returns by ratio rather than by absolute sum.
items.cn: profitability 出现在十九世纪的商业写作中，当时企业开始用比率而非绝对金额比较回报。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word became a standard heading in financial analysis, management targets and sector studies.
items.cn: 在二十世纪，这个词成为财务分析、管理目标与行业研究中的标准条目。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first citation of profitability is not established, and the pre-Latin root of the verb behind profit is reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：profitability 的确切最早书证未得到证明，profit 背后那个动词在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds the adjective, the noun of gain and the measured noun, which are constantly swapped; group two holds other measures of financial health.
note.cn: 第一组是形容词、表示增益的名词与表示计量结果的名词，常被互换误用；第二组是其他衡量财务健康的概念。

entries.definition: Says that something yields a gain; the noun names the capacity or its measured level.
entries.definitionCN: 说某物能带来收益；名词则指这种能力或其计量水平。

entries.definition: The gain itself in money; profitability is the ability or degree, not the sum.
entries.definitionCN: 指金钱上的增益本身；profitability 是能力或程度，不是金额。

entries.definition: Describes how an action is performed; it cannot serve as the subject of a sentence about performance.
entries.definitionCN: 描述动作如何执行；不能充当讨论业绩的句子主语。

entries.definition: The practice of taking excessive gain, especially in a shortage; it carries blame that profitability does not.
entries.definitionCN: 指在短缺等情况下牟取过厚利润的做法；带谴责意味，而 profitability 没有。

entries.definition: The gain on an investment as a proportion of what was put in; it can refer to a single asset rather than a whole business.
entries.definitionCN: 投资收益占投入的比例；可指单项资产，而非整个企业。

entries.definition: The part of each sale that is kept as profit; a narrower measure than profitability.
entries.definitionCN: 每笔销售中留作利润的部分；比盈利能力更窄的指标。

entries.definition: The ratio of output to input; a firm can be efficient and still unprofitable if prices are too low.
entries.definitionCN: 产出与投入之比；企业可以很高效，却因价格过低而无利可图。

entries.definition: The ability to meet debts as they fall due; it concerns survival, not surplus.
entries.definitionCN: 到期偿还债务的能力；关乎生存，而非盈余。

entries.definition: The ability of an organisation or plan to survive; profitability adds the requirement of a surplus.
entries.definitionCN: 组织或计划维持下去的能力；盈利能力则额外要求有盈余。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix chain, the real accounting phrases and the real distinction from the sum itself.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的后缀链条、真实会计搭配，以及它与金额本身的真实区别。

normal.en: Profitable plus the suffix of quality gives the name of the quality: the ability to earn a surplus.
normal.cn: profitable 加表示性质的后缀，就得到这种性质的名字：赚取盈余的能力。

normal.en: The family runs profit, profitable, profitability, profitably, unprofitable.
normal.cn: 词族包括 profit、profitable、profitability、profitably、unprofitable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the analysis: profitability ratio, profitability analysis, long-term profitability.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出分析语境：盈利能力比率、盈利能力分析、长期盈利能力。

normal.en: Profit is a number; profitability is a rate or a capacity.
normal.cn: 利润是一个数字；盈利能力是一种比率或能力。

normal.en: A firm can post a profit and still have weak profitability if its capital is huge.
normal.cn: 一家企业可以录得利润，若资本庞大，盈利能力仍然偏弱。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid across a report to show how much each unit of money brings back.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子横放在报表上，量出每一单位钱能带回多少。

abstract.en: Picture a plant that keeps producing fruit year after year without being replanted.
abstract.cn: 想象一株植物年年结果，而无需重新栽种。

abstract.en: Picture a scale that compares what a workshop consumes with what it sends out.
abstract.cn: 想象一杆秤，比较一间作坊消耗的东西与它送出的东西。

examples.en: The merger was intended to lift profitability rather than to cut jobs.
examples.cn: 这次合并意在提高盈利能力，而非裁减岗位。

examples.en: Farm profitability depends heavily on the price of fuel.
examples.cn: 农业的盈利能力在很大程度上取决于燃料价格。

examples.en: They measured profitability per hectare rather than per worker.
examples.cn: 他们按每公顷而非每名工人衡量盈利能力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「profit（利润）＋表示『能力』的后缀」——能持续赚出利润的本事，就是盈利能力

root: profitable（profit 来自拉丁语 profectus「增益」，加表「能够」的后缀）＋一个源自拉丁语、表示性质或状态的后缀（拉丁语 -itas）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one question: how well does this pay? The question is asked of a capacity, a measured level, a ratio, a target, a sector, a long horizon, a single product line and finally of any arrangement that returns more than it consumes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个问题展开：这件事有多划算？问题依次指向一种能力、一个计量水平、一项比率、一个目标、一个行业、一段长期、一条产品线，最后指向任何回报高于消耗的安排。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler laid across accounts to measure what each unit of money brings back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把尺子横在账目上，量出每一单位钱能带回多少。

branches.en: CAPACITY AND LEVEL: the quality exists first as an ability, then as a figure that rises or falls.
branches.cn: 能力与水平：这种性质先作为能力存在，再作为一个会升会降的数字存在。

branches.en: RATIO: to compare firms of different size, the ability is expressed as a proportion.
branches.cn: 比率：为比较规模不同的企业，这种能力被表示成比例。

branches.en: TARGET: a measured quality can be aimed at, so description becomes an objective.
branches.cn: 目标：可计量的性质能成为瞄准的对象，描述于是变成目标。

branches.en: UNIT OF ANALYSIS: the same measure is applied to a whole sector and to a single product line.
branches.cn: 分析单元：同一项度量既用于整个行业，也用于单条产品线。

branches.en: TIME AND GENERALITY: durability adds a long horizon, and the idea finally leaves money behind.
branches.cn: 时间与泛化：持久性加上长期维度，这个观念最终离开金钱语境。

intro.en: The noun stacks three pieces: a Latin participle turned noun, a suffix of capacity, and a suffix of quality.
intro.cn: 这个名词叠了三层：拉丁分词转成的名词、表示能力的后缀，以及表示性质的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin profectus supplies profit, Latin -abilis supplies the adjective ending, and Latin -itas supplies the final noun ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 profectus 提供 profit，拉丁语 -abilis 提供形容词词尾，拉丁语 -itas 提供最终的名词词尾。

items.example: The prefix gives the direction of gain.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给出增益的方向。
这个词根构成 profit 的基础。
这条产品线是有利可图的。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成一种性质。
这支船队以获利的方式运营。

items.example: The branch was unprofitable for years.
items.exampleCN: 这个分支多年无利可图。

definition_zh: 病理的；病态的；反常到近乎病态的
definition_en: of a disease, or of behaviour that seems to obey a disease rather than a will
core_image: 一片组织放到显微镜下，被放大到能看见病变的那一层
scene: 病理科把切片放到镜下，那层变化不因谁的看法而改变。 The slide showed a pathological change that no argument could wish away.
sceneCN: 这里 pathological 指病理上的改变（第 1 个义项：病理学的）；句意为镜下切片显出病理性的变化，任何争辩都无法把它抹去。

pos.zh: 病理的；病态的；反常到近乎病态的

senses.title: Of disease
senses.definition: belonging to the study of disease or to a disease itself
senses.definitionCN: 属于疾病研究，或属于某种疾病本身
senses.example: The report described a pathological lesion in the lung.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了肺部的一处病理病变。
senses.why: This is the technical sense doctors use every day.
senses.whyCN: 这是医生每天在用的技术义。

senses.title: Pathological liar
senses.definition: of a person who lies so often that lying no longer looks like a choice
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人说谎频繁到说谎已不像一种选择
senses.example: Her brother was a pathological liar who could not stop at the truth.
senses.exampleCN: 她弟弟是个病态说谎者，讲到真话也停不下来。
senses.why: Here the word moves from tissue to habit and still sounds clinical.
senses.whyCN: 这里词从组织移向习惯，却仍带着临床口吻。

senses.title: Pathological fear
senses.definition: of a fear far beyond the danger that caused it
senses.definitionCN: 形容恐惧远远超过引起它的危险
senses.example: He had a pathological fear of lifts and took the stairs for years.
senses.exampleCN: 他对电梯有病理性的恐惧，多年都走楼梯。
senses.why: The fear is real, but its size has no proportion to its cause.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧是真的，但它的规模与原因完全不成比例。

senses.title: Pathological gambling
senses.definition: of an impulse to gamble that overruns money, family and sleep
senses.definitionCN: 形容赌博冲动压过金钱、家庭与睡眠
senses.example: The clinic treated pathological gambling as an addiction, not a vice.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所把病态赌博当作成瘾，而不是恶习。
senses.why: The word moves the blame from character to condition.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把责备从人品移到病症。

senses.title: Pathological jealousy
senses.definition: of a suspicion that feeds on itself and needs no evidence
senses.definitionCN: 形容自我滋养、不需要证据的猜疑
senses.example: Pathological jealousy turned every late train into proof.
senses.exampleCN: 病态的嫉妒把每一班晚点列车都变成证据。
senses.why: Nothing can disprove it, which is exactly what makes it pathological.
senses.whyCN: 什么都无法反驳它，而这正是它病态之处。

senses.title: Of tissue
senses.definition: of a specimen examined for signs of disease rather than for normal structure
senses.definitionCN: 形容标本检查的是疾病迹象，而非正常结构
senses.example: The pathological specimen was kept in the teaching collection.
senses.exampleCN: 那份病理标本被保存在教学收藏里。
senses.why: Medical schools name a thing by what it shows, and this specimen shows illness.
senses.whyCN: 医学院按它显示的东西命名，而这份标本显示的是病。

senses.title: Beyond reason
senses.definition: of behaviour so fixed that argument cannot move it
senses.definitionCN: 形容行为僵硬到争论无法撼动
senses.example: His pathological punctuality made every delay feel like an insult.
senses.exampleCN: 他那近乎病态的守时，让每一次延误都像侮辱。
senses.why: The joke works because the word exaggerates a virtue into a symptom.
senses.whyCN: 这个玩笑成立，因为这个词把一种美德夸张成了症状。

senses.title: As a metaphor
senses.definition: of any habit described as if it were a disease, usually with disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 形容任何被当作疾病来描述的习惯，通常带着不赞许
senses.example: Critics called the party's pathological optimism a refusal to read the polls.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者把该党病态的乐观称为拒绝看民调。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows a doctor's authority to win an argument.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借来医生的权威，用来赢下一场争论。

intro.en: Pathological began at the bedside: pathos is Greek for what a body suffers, and -logia is the study of it.
intro.cn: pathological 从病床边开始：pathos 在希腊语里指身体所受的苦，-logia 是对它的研究。

items.en: Pathos meant 'suffering, disease, feeling', a word that always points at something endured.
items.cn: pathos 意为「痛苦、疾病、情感」，这个词总是指向某种被承受的东西。

items.en: -Logia meant 'study, account', the ending behind biology and theology.
items.cn: -logia 意为「研究、论述」，是 biology 与 theology 背后的词尾。

items.en: The compound pathologia named the study of disease in learned Latin.
items.cn: 复合词 pathologia 在学术拉丁语里指对疾病的研究。

items.en: English took pathology in the seventeenth century, and the adjective pathological followed it.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 pathology，形容词 pathological 随之而来。

items.en: Later centuries extended the word from tissue to habits and feelings judged beyond reason.
items.cn: 后来的世纪把这个词从组织扩展到被判为超出理性的习惯与情绪。

note.en: The look-alike group is the pathos family; the near-meaning group separates disease, compulsion and mere strangeness.
note.cn: 形近组是 pathos 词族；近义组把「疾病」「强迫」与「只是古怪」分开。

entries.definition: the study of disease.
entries.definitionCN: 对疾病的研究。

entries.definition: a doctor who reads tissue for disease.
entries.definitionCN: 通过组织判读疾病的医生。

entries.definition: in a way that belongs to disease.
entries.definitionCN: 以属于疾病的方式。

entries.definition: a germ that causes disease.
entries.definitionCN: 引起疾病的病原体。

entries.definition: affected by illness.
entries.definitionCN: 受疾病影响的。

entries.definition: fixated on disease or death.
entries.definitionCN: 执迷于疾病或死亡的。

entries.definition: driven by an urge one cannot resist.
entries.definitionCN: 被无法抵抗的冲动驱使的。

entries.definition: departing from the usual order.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离通常秩序的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a slide under a lens, where what the body hid becomes visible.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「切片放到镜下、身体藏起的东西显形」的画面。

normal.en: Pathological holds pathos, Greek for suffering; the word always points at something a body or mind endures.
normal.cn: pathological 里藏着 pathos（希腊语的受苦）；这个词总指向身体或心智所承受的东西。

normal.en: Think of a slide under a microscope: the trouble is at the level of tissue, not opinion.
normal.cn: 想象镜下的一张切片：问题在组织那一层，不在看法那一层。

normal.en: Pa-tho-LO-gi-cal: put the stress on LO, where the study of disease sits.
normal.cn: pa-tho-LO-gi-cal：重音落在 LO，正是疾病研究所在。

normal.en: Say path-uh-LOJ-i-kl; the ending -logical names a field, not a patient.
normal.cn: 读成 path-uh-LOJ-i-kl，词尾 -logical 命名的是一个领域，不是病人。

normal.en: Pair it with liar and gambler: the word turns a habit into a diagnosis.
normal.cn: 把它和 liar、gambler 配对：这个词把习惯变成了诊断。

abstract.en: A word that began in the morgue ends up in arguments about habits, because both involve something that will not answer reason.
abstract.cn: 一个从停尸房开始的词，最后进了关于习惯的争论，因为两者都涉及某种不回应理性的东西。

abstract.en: Calling a behaviour pathological is a polite way of saying it has stopped being a choice.
abstract.cn: 把一种行为称为病态，是「它已不再是选择」的礼貌说法。

abstract.en: The word's authority is medical; its most common work is moral.
abstract.cn: 这个词的权威来自医学，它最常干的活却是道德评判。

examples.en: The slide showed a pathological change that no argument could wish away.
examples.cn: 镜下显出病理性的变化，任何争辩都无法把它抹去。

examples.en: The clinic treated pathological gambling as an addiction, not a vice.
examples.cn: 诊所把病态赌博当作成瘾，而不是恶习。

examples.en: His pathological punctuality made every delay feel like an insult.
examples.cn: 他那近乎病态的守时，让每一次延误都像侮辱。

dict_mnemonic.text: patho（病）+ logical（逻辑）：按病灶的逻辑行事，就是「病态的」。

root: 希腊语 pathos（痛苦、疾病）与 -logia（学说），经拉丁语 pathologia 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses begin at the microscope and end at the dinner table: tissue, lying, fear, gambling, jealousy, a specimen, punctuality and a party's optimism.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从显微镜下开始，到餐桌上结束：组织、说谎、恐惧、赌博、嫉妒、标本、守时与一个政党的乐观。

core.en: A SLIDE THAT SHOWS WHAT THE BODY HIDES
core.cn: 镜下显出身体藏起来的那一层

branches.en: The clinic and the specimen.
branches.cn: 诊所与标本。

branches.en: Lying and fear, habits wearing a symptom's shape.
branches.cn: 说谎与恐惧，带着症状形状的习惯。

branches.en: Gambling and jealousy, appetites that feed themselves.
branches.cn: 赌博与嫉妒，自我喂养的欲望。

branches.en: Punctuality pushed past the edge of virtue.
branches.cn: 被推过美德边界的守时。

branches.en: The metaphor borrowed for an argument.
branches.cn: 为一场争论借来的比喻。

intro.en: The pathos family is about what is suffered: pathology studies it, a pathogen causes it, sympathy feels it with another person.
intro.cn: pathos 词族关乎被承受的苦：pathology 研究它，pathogen 引起它，sympathy 与另一个人一同感受它。

latinIntro.en: Greek pathos supplies the suffering and -logia supplies the study; the prefixes syn- and a- only decide whether the feeling is shared or absent.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 pathos 提供苦，-logia 提供研究；前缀 syn- 与 a- 只决定这份感受是被分担还是缺席。

definition_zh: 幼虫；昆虫自卵孵化后的幼期形态；毛虫、蛆、蛴螬等幼体；水生无脊椎动物的自由生活幼体；蝌蚪式的水生幼期；生命史中的幼体阶段；不成熟的雏形；面具与幽灵（拉丁语旧义）
definition_en: the immature feeding stage of an insect or other invertebrate, which later changes into the adult form; historically also a mask or ghost
core_image: 叶片背面趴着一条肉虫，身体一节一节，六只真足紧贴叶脉，身边是被啃出的缺口
scene: 叶片背面，一条幼虫紧贴叶脉啃出月牙形的缺口。 A larva chews a crescent hole in the leaf while clinging to the vein.
sceneCN: 这里 larva 指「昆虫自卵孵化后的幼期取食形态」（第 1 个义项：幼虫）；句意为一条幼虫紧贴叶脉、在叶片上啃出月牙形缺口。可辨识物件：分节体躯、六只真足、叶脉、月牙形缺口。

pos.zh: 幼虫；幼体（昆虫或其它无脊椎动物）

senses.title: The immature feeding stage of an insect
senses.titleCN: 昆虫自卵孵化后的取食幼期
senses.definition: the wingless, often worm-like stage that hatches from an egg and feeds before transforming
senses.definitionCN: 从卵中孵出、通常无翅且形似蠕虫、取食之后才转变的幼期
senses.example: A larva chews a crescent hole in the leaf while clinging to the vein.
senses.exampleCN: 一条幼虫紧贴叶脉，在叶片上啃出月牙形缺口。
senses.why: The word marks a stage, not a species: any insect that undergoes complete change passes through a larva before the pupa.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标的是阶段而非物种：任何完全变态的昆虫都要经过幼虫才到蛹。

senses.title: A caterpillar or grub
senses.titleCN: 毛虫、蛆、蛴螬等具体幼体
senses.definition: the familiar worm-like young of butterflies, beetles or flies, named by shape in everyday speech
senses.definitionCN: 蝴蝶、甲虫或蝇类的幼体，日常说法按形状称呼
senses.example: The caterpillar is the larva of a moth or butterfly.
senses.exampleCN: 毛虫是蛾或蝴蝶的幼虫。
senses.why: Everyday names such as grub, maggot and caterpillar split the general stage into recognizable shapes.
senses.whyCN: 蛴螬、蛆、毛虫这些日常名把笼统的幼期拆成可辨认的形状。

senses.title: The free-living young of water animals
senses.titleCN: 水生无脊椎动物的自由生活幼体
senses.definition: a swimming young stage of many marine invertebrates, such as the trochophore of a worm or the nauplius of a crustacean
senses.definitionCN: 许多海洋无脊椎动物的游泳幼期，如环节动物的担轮幼虫或甲壳类的无节幼虫
senses.example: The barnacle passes through a swimming larva before it settles.
senses.exampleCN: 藤壶在定居之前要经过一个游泳的幼体阶段。
senses.why: Zoology generalized the term from insects to any animal whose young differs sharply from the adult.
senses.whyCN: 动物学把这个词从昆虫扩大到任何幼体与成体差别很大的动物。

senses.title: The tadpole stage of amphibians
senses.titleCN: 两栖类的水生幼期（蝌蚪）
senses.definition: the aquatic, gilled young of a frog or salamander, which later metamorphoses into the adult
senses.definitionCN: 蛙或蝾螈具鳃的水生幼体，之后变态为成体
senses.example: The tadpole is the larva of a frog, and it breathes with gills.
senses.exampleCN: 蝌蚪是蛙的幼虫，用鳃呼吸。
senses.why: Amphibian biology borrowed the insect term because the same two-stage pattern appears, water young then land adult.
senses.whyCN: 两栖动物学借用了昆虫术语，因为出现了同样的两段式格局：水中幼体，陆生成体。

senses.title: A stage in a life cycle
senses.definition: the phase of a life cycle entered after hatching and left at metamorphosis, treated as a unit of timing
senses.definitionCN: 孵化之后进入、变态时结束的生命史阶段，被当作计时单位
senses.example: Larvae feed for weeks before the pupal stage begins.
senses.exampleCN: 幼虫取食数周之后才进入蛹期。
senses.why: This abstract sense measures development by stages; the noun becomes a slot in a schedule rather than an animal.
senses.whyCN: 这一抽象义用阶段来度量发育；名词成了时间表上的格子，而非动物。

senses.title: An undeveloped early form
senses.definition: anything that exists in an early, unformed state, compared to an insect that has not yet taken its adult shape
senses.definitionCN: 任何处于早期、尚未成形状态的事物，比作尚未长成成虫形态的昆虫
senses.example: The proposal is still a larva, all appetite and no structure.
senses.exampleCN: 这份提案还只是个幼虫，只有胃口，没有结构。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the biological core: what is describes is feeding and growing, not yet finished.
senses.whyCN: 比喻保留了生物核心：所描述之物正在取食与生长，尚未完成。

senses.title: A mask or ghost
senses.definition: the original Latin sense of a mask, especially one worn by an actor, or a ghost haunting a house
senses.definitionCN: 拉丁语原义：面具，尤指演员所戴，或出没于屋中的幽灵
senses.example: In Latin, larva could mean a mask worn on the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 在拉丁语中，larva 可以指舞台上戴的面具。
senses.why: Linnaeus took an old word for mask and ghost and made it a scientific term, so the modern sense carries a trace of disguise.
senses.whyCN: 林奈把一个意为面具与幽灵的旧词变成科学术语，现代义因此带着伪装的痕迹。

senses.title: A juvenile form used as food or pest
senses.titleCN: 作为饵料或害虫的幼体
senses.definition: the young stage considered as a resource or a pest, as when larvae are sold as fish food or sprayed as crop pests
senses.definitionCN: 把幼期当作资源或害物，如作为鱼饲料出售或作为作物害虫喷杀
senses.example: Anglers buy larvae by the tub for bait.
senses.exampleCN: 钓鱼人按盒购买幼虫作饵。
senses.why: Economics and agriculture recast the stage as a product or a target, which is a further extension of the biological sense.
senses.whyCN: 经济与农业把这个阶段改读为产品或清除对象，是生物义的进一步延伸。

intro.en: Larva is Latin for 'mask, ghost'. Linnaeus adopted it in the eighteenth century for the young stage of an insect, and the entomological sense drove out the older one.
intro.cn: larva 在拉丁语中意为「面具、幽灵」。林奈在 18 世纪把它采用为昆虫幼期的名称，昆虫学义后来压过了旧义。

items.en: Latin larva meant a mask, especially a frightening one, and by extension a ghost or spectre.
items.cn: 拉丁 larva 指面具，尤指吓人的面具，并引申为幽灵、鬼魂。

items.en: Latin plural larvae came into English with the scientific term; the English plural larvas is rare and mainly historical.
items.cn: 拉丁复数 larvae 随科学术语进入英语；英语式复数 larvas 罕见，主要用于历史文献。

items.en: The step from 'mask' to 'caterpillar' is not fully explained; a common suggestion is that the young insect looks like a disguise of the adult, but this is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 从「面具」到「毛虫」的一步没有得到完整解释；常见说法是幼体看起来像成虫的伪装，但这只是假说。

items.en: Linnaeus fixed larva as the term for the immature stage in his eighteenth-century classification, and the word entered general English through natural history.
items.cn: 林奈在 18 世纪分类学中把 larva 定为幼期的术语，这个词经自然史著作进入一般英语。

items.en: Zoology later applied the term to the young of crustaceans, molluscs and amphibians, widening it well beyond insects.
items.cn: 动物学后来把这个词用于甲壳类、软体动物与两栖类的幼体，范围远超昆虫。

items.en: Source uncertain (detail and first date): the deeper origin and the exact first citation are not settled, so any pre-Latin form offered here is a reconstruction and competing hypotheses are left side by side.
items.cn: 来源不确定（细节与首见年代）：更深的来源与确切最早书证均无定论，此处给出的拉丁语之前形式属重构形式，并列假说一并保留、不作定论。

note.en: Group one holds words whose spelling or sound invites confusion with larva; group two holds biological terms for young animals.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音易与 larva 混淆的词；第二组收表示幼体动物的生物学术语。

entries.definition: Lava comes from Italian and Latin labes 'a fall, a slide' and has nothing to do with insects; the two words differ by one letter.
entries.definitionCN: lava 来自意大利语与拉丁 labes「滑落」，与昆虫无关；两词只差一个字母。

entries.definition: Larval is the adjective built on larva, not a separate noun.
entries.definitionCN: larval 是由 larva 构成的形容词，不是另一个名词。

entries.definition: Larvae is simply the Latin plural of larva; using it as a singular is a common error.
entries.definitionCN: larvae 只是 larva 的拉丁复数；把它当单数用是常见错误。

entries.definition: This English-style plural appears in older texts but is not the standard form today.
entries.definitionCN: 这一英语式复数见于较早文献，今天并非标准形式。

entries.definition: A nymph is the young of an insect with incomplete metamorphosis; it already resembles the adult and has no pupal stage.
entries.definitionCN: nymph 指不完全变态昆虫的幼期；它已形似成虫，没有蛹期。

entries.definition: A grub is a thick, legless larva, typically of a beetle, and names one shape rather than the stage.
entries.definitionCN: grub 指粗壮无足的幼虫，多见于甲虫，是一个形状名称而非阶段名称。

entries.definition: Caterpillar names the larva of a butterfly or moth, usually with visible legs and a segmented body.
entries.definitionCN: caterpillar 指蝴蝶或蛾的幼虫，通常有明显足与分节的身体。

entries.definition: A maggot is the legless larva of a fly, found in decaying matter and used in medicine to clean wounds.
entries.definitionCN: maggot 是蝇类的无足幼虫，见于腐败物中，医学上也用于清创。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin larva first meant a mask or ghost; the insect sense is a later scientific borrowing.
normal.cn: 拉丁 larva 本指面具或幽灵；昆虫义是后来的科学借用。

normal.en: The family runs larva, larvae, larval, larvicide and larviparous.
normal.cn: 词族包括 larva、larvae、larval、larvicide 与 larviparous。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: larva stage, insect larva, larva migrans.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：幼虫期、昆虫幼虫、游走性幼虫。

normal.en: The standard plural is larvae, following Latin first-declension nouns.
normal.cn: 标准复数是 larvae，遵循拉丁第一变格法名词。

normal.en: Complete metamorphosis runs egg, larva, pupa, adult.
normal.cn: 完全变态依次为卵、幼虫、蛹、成虫。

abstract.en: Picture a mask left on a chair, still shaped like the face that wore it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张留在椅子上的面具，仍带着戴它那张脸的轮廓。

abstract.en: Picture a body that is all appetite and no wings.
abstract.cn: 想象一具只有胃口、没有翅膀的身体。

abstract.en: Picture a swimmer that will later glue itself to a rock and never move again.
abstract.cn: 想象一个游泳者，日后会把自己粘在岩石上，再也不动。

examples.en: Each larva moults several times before it is ready to pupate.
examples.cn: 每条幼虫在准备化蛹前要蜕皮数次。

examples.en: The larvae of mosquitoes breathe through a tube at the water surface.
examples.cn: 蚊的幼虫通过水面上的呼吸管呼吸。

examples.en: Fossil larvae show the feeding marks of ancient insects on leaves.
examples.cn: 化石幼虫在叶片上留下了远古昆虫的取食痕迹。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「larva（拉瓦）」——从卵里「拉」出来的小肉虫 → 幼虫

root: 拉丁 larva「面具、幽灵」；林奈 18 世纪采用为昆虫幼期术语。「面具」到「毛虫」的过渡未获完整解释，相关说法仅为假说。复数 larvae 为拉丁式，larvas 罕见。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses trace one stage: a worm-like feeder, its named shapes, its water-borne cousins, the amphibian version, the slot in a life cycle, the metaphor of immaturity, the old mask sense and the stage as product.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个阶段展开：蠕虫状的取食者、各种形状名称、水中同族、两栖版本、生命史中的一格、不成熟的比喻、旧时的面具义，以及作为产品的幼体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a segmented worm-like body with six true legs clamped to a leaf vein, eating a crescent hole.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具分节的蠕虫状身体，六只真足扣住叶脉，啃出月牙形缺口。

branches.en: THE FEEDER: the stage and its everyday shapes, caterpillar, grub and maggot.
branches.cn: 取食者：这一阶段及其日常形状——毛虫、蛴螬、蛆。

branches.en: OTHER WATERS: crustacean and amphibian young repeat the pattern outside insects.
branches.cn: 别处的水域：甲壳类与两栖类的幼体在昆虫之外重复同一格局。

branches.en: THE SLOT: life cycle timing turns the animal into a stage and a product.
branches.cn: 那一格：生命史的计时把动物变成阶段与产品。

branches.en: IMMATURE FORM: the metaphor keeps feeding and growing, without a finished shape.
branches.cn: 未成形：比喻保留取食与生长，尚无完成的形状。

branches.en: MASK AND GHOST: the Latin word for a disguise is the origin of the scientific term.
branches.cn: 面具与幽灵：意为伪装的那个拉丁词正是科学术语的来源。

intro.en: Larva is a Latin noun; English builds its family with Latin plurals and suffixes, and the larv- stem also appears in learned compounds.
intro.cn: larva 是拉丁名词；英语用拉丁复数与后缀构成词族，larv- 词干也出现在学术复合词中。

latinIntro.en: Latin larva, plural larvae, gives larval, larvicide and larviparous; the same stem appears in larvarium, a place for keeping larvae.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 larva（复数 larvae）衍生 larval、larvicide、larviparous；同一词干亦见于 larvarium，指饲养幼虫的场所。

items.example: Each larva feeds on one leaf.
items.exampleCN: 每条幼虫取食一片叶子。

items.example: The larvae hatch within three days.
The pond was treated with a larvicide.
Some flies are larviparous rather than egg-laying.
items.exampleCN: 有些蝇类直接产幼虫而非产卵。

items.example: The female beetle remains larviform as an adult.
items.exampleCN: 这种雌甲虫成年后仍保持幼虫形。

items.example: The lab keeps a larvarium beside the microscope.
items.exampleCN: 实验室在显微镜旁设了幼虫饲养箱。

items.example: Larva migrans produces a creeping skin line.
items.exampleCN: 游走性幼虫在皮肤上留下爬行线。

latinEntries.structure: larva, larvae (f., first declension, zoological use)
latinEntries.meaning: the young stage of an animal

definition_zh: 交替；轮流；使交替发生（形容词：交替的；间隔的；备选的）
definition_en: to take place by turns, or (of things) occurring by turns; every other one; a substitute
core_image: 左右脚一步一步轮流落地
scene: 红灯绿灯按节奏轮流亮起。 Red and green lights alternate at the crossing.
sceneCN: 这里的 alternate 是「交替」（第 1 个义项：按次序轮流出现）；句意是路口的红绿灯轮流亮起。

pos.zh: 交替；轮流；使交替
交替的；间隔的；备选的
替代者；候补者

derivatives.zh: 由 alternate 加 -ion 构成，义为「交替；轮换」
现在分词形容词，义为「交替的」
同根词，义为「选择；可选的」，侧重「替代选项」
由 alternate 加 -ly 构成，义为「交替地」

senses.title: To occur by turns
senses.definition: to happen one after the other in a repeating two-part pattern
senses.definitionCN: 以两部分重复的次序先后发生
senses.example: Days of rain alternated with bright mornings.
senses.exampleCN: 雨天与晴朗的早晨交替出现。
senses.why: The Latin alternus means "one after the other": two things taking turns.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 alternus 意为「一个接一个」：两物轮换。

senses.title: To cause to take turns
senses.definition: to arrange for two things or people to follow each other in turn
senses.definitionCN: 安排两事物或两人依次轮换
senses.example: The coach alternated the two goalkeepers.
senses.exampleCN: 教练让两名门将轮换上场。
senses.why: The transitive use arranges the same taking of turns.
senses.whyCN: 及物用法就是安排这种轮换。

senses.title: Occurring every other one
senses.definition: happening on every second occasion, skipping one
senses.definitionCN: 每两次发生一次，跳过一次
senses.example: The market is open on alternate Saturdays.
senses.exampleCN: 市场每隔一个周六开市。
senses.why: With only two slots, taking turns means every other one.
senses.whyCN: 只有两个位置时，轮换就意味着每隔一个。

senses.title: Placed one after the other
senses.definition: of things in a row, following one another in a repeating pattern
senses.definitionCN: 一列事物按重复模式依次排列
senses.example: Alternate stripes of black and white.
senses.exampleCN: 黑白相间的条纹。
senses.why: The turn-taking pattern frozen into an arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 轮换模式凝固成排列方式。

senses.title: Serving as a substitute
senses.definition: available or used in place of the usual one
senses.definitionCN: 可替代通常事物或供其代替使用的
senses.example: They found an alternate route around the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 他们找到一条绕过洪水的替代路线。
senses.why: The one who takes the other turn is the substitute.
senses.whyCN: 轮到另一次的那个就是替代者。

senses.title: A person who substitutes
senses.definition: a person ready to act in place of another, as an alternate delegate
senses.definitionCN: 准备顶替他人的人，如候补代表
senses.example: She attended the board as an alternate.
senses.exampleCN: 她以候补身份参加了董事会。
senses.why: The substitute sense becomes a noun for the person.
senses.whyCN: 替代义转为指人的名词。

senses.title: Reciprocal or mutual action
senses.definition: of actions exchanged back and forth between two parties
senses.definitionCN: 两方之间往复交换的动作
senses.example: The negotiators alternate offers and rebuttals.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判者轮流出价与反驳。
senses.why: Taking turns implies exchange; the turn returns.
senses.whyCN: 轮换暗含交换：这一轮还会回来。

senses.title: Alternating current sense
senses.definition: of electric current, reversing direction periodically, as in alternating current
senses.definitionCN: 指电流周期性反向，如交流电
senses.example: Household power is alternating current.
senses.exampleCN: 家用电是交流电。
senses.why: The turn-taking pattern applied to the direction of flow.
senses.whyCN: 轮换模式应用于电流方向。

intro.en: Alternate comes from Latin alternare, "to do by turns", from alternus "one after the other".
intro.cn: alternate 源自拉丁语 alternare「轮换着做」，来自 alternus「一个接一个」。

items.en: Root *al-, "beyond, other", the same root behind alias and alien.
items.cn: 重构词根 *al-「另一、其他」，也是 alias、alien 的词根。

items.en: alter "the other of two" → alternus "by turns" → alternare "to alternate".
items.cn: 拉丁语 alter「两者中的另一个」→ alternus「轮流的」→ alternare「交替」。

items.en: alternare used in ecclesiastical and legal Latin.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 alternare 用于教会与法律拉丁语。

items.en: alterner, the learned borrowing channel.
items.cn: 古法语 alterner，学术借入通道。

items.en: alternate adopted as verb and adjective.
items.cn: alternate 以动词与形容词进入英语。

items.en: Verb stress on -nate; adjective stress fronted; a noun sense for substitutes.
items.cn: 动词重音在 -nate，形容词重音前移，另有指候补者的名词义。

note.en: Alternate and alternative are siblings from alter with divided jobs, and alternate alternates with itself in pronunciation.
note.cn: alternate 与 alternative 是 alter 的孪生词、分工不同；alternate 一词本身兼有两种发音。

entries.definition: a choice or option; the sibling word now preferred for "substitute" in American usage.
entries.definitionCN: 选择、选项；表示「替代」时美式用法更倾向此词。

entries.definition: to change; the base verb of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 改变；词族的基干动词。

entries.definition: a dispute; "othering" each other in argument.
entries.definitionCN: 争执；在争论中互为「对方」。

entries.definition: to take turns in a cycle, often of more than two.
entries.definitionCN: 轮换，常指多于两者。

entries.definition: to give back in return; the exchange side of alternation.
entries.definitionCN: 回报；交替中的交换面。

entries.definition: to switch places or exchange repeatedly.
entries.definitionCN: 反复互换。

normalIntro.en: Remember alternate as alter's turn-taking twin.
normalIntro.cn: 把 alternate 记成 alter 的「轮换」孪生词。

normal.en: alter "the other of two" + -nate: taking the other turn.
normal.cn: alter「两者中的另一个」+ -nate：轮到另一次。

normal.en: Pronunciation: verb al-ter-NAYT, adjective AL-ter-nit.
normal.cn: 发音：动词 al-ter-NAYT，形容词 AL-ter-nit。

normal.en: Family: alter, alteration, alternative, altercation, alternation.
normal.cn: 词族：alter、alteration、alternative、altercation、alternation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: alternating current, alternate days, alternate route.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：alternating current、alternate days、alternate route。

normal.en: Picture walking: left, right, left, right — the feet alternate.
normal.cn: 画面：走路时左右脚轮流—— feet alternate。

abstract.en: A seesaw tilting left, right, left.
abstract.cn: 跷跷板左、右、左地倾斜。

abstract.en: Two chat bubbles appearing one after the other.
abstract.cn: 两个聊天气泡一先一后出现。

abstract.en: A chess clock slapped in turn by two players.
abstract.cn: 两位棋手轮流拍按棋钟。

examples.en: The two hosts alternate each week.
examples.cn: 两位主持人每周轮换。

examples.en: Take an alternate road to avoid the jam.
examples.cn: 换条替代路线避开拥堵。

examples.en: Hope and fear alternated in her letters.
examples.cn: 希望与恐惧在她的信中交替出现。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特内特」——奥特（alter）是“另一个”，内特（-nate）是“轮到”，另一个轮到就是交替。

root: 拉丁语 alter「两者中的另一个」（印欧词根 *al-「其他」）派生 alternus「轮流的」、动词 alternare「交替」，经古法语 alterner 于十五六世纪进入英语；同根词 alternative、altercation、altruist。

sensesIntro.en: From two things taking turns, the senses cover causing turns, skipping every other, alternating arrangements, substitutes for things and people, reciprocal exchange, and periodic reversal in current.
sensesIntro.cn: 从两物轮换出发，义项覆盖使轮换、每隔一次、相间排列、物与人的替代、往复交换，以及电流的周期反向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two of a kind taking turns
core.cn: 核心意象：同类两者轮流登场

branches.en: Turns occurring and being arranged.
branches.cn: 轮换的发生与安排。

branches.en: Every-other occurrence and alternating arrangement.
branches.cn: 间隔发生与相间排列。

branches.en: Substitutes, whether things or persons.
branches.cn: 物或人的替代。

branches.en: Back-and-forth exchange.
branches.cn: 往复交换。

branches.en: Periodic reversal, as in alternating current.
branches.cn: 周期反向，如交流电。

intro.en: Alternate is built on alter with Latin verb endings.
intro.cn: alternate 以 alter 为基干加拉丁动词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: The whole family descends from one small Latin word meaning "the other".
latinIntro.cn: 整个词族都源于一个意为「另一个」的拉丁小词。

definition_zh: 黄铁矿；愚人金
definition_en: a yellow metallic mineral that looks like gold but is iron sulphide
core_image: 淘金者捧着闪亮的石头，以为发了财，其实是黄铁矿
scene: 淘金者以为自己发现了金矿，其实那只是黄铁矿。 The prospector thought he had struck gold, but the glitter was only pyrite.
sceneCN: 这里 pyrite 指黄铁矿（第 1 个义项：黄铁矿）；句意为淘金者以为自己发现了金矿，其实那只是黄铁矿。

pos.zh: 黄铁矿；愚人金

senses.title: The mineral
senses.definition: a hard yellow mineral made of iron and sulphur
senses.definitionCN: 由铁与硫构成的坚硬黄色矿物
senses.example: The prospector thought he had struck gold, but the glitter was only pyrite.
senses.exampleCN: 淘金者以为自己发现了金矿，但那点闪光只是黄铁矿。
senses.why: The first sense is the plain mineralogical one.
senses.whyCN: 第一个义项是最朴素的矿物学义项。

senses.title: Fool's gold
senses.definition: the popular name for pyrite because it deceives the eye
senses.definitionCN: 因能骗过眼睛而得的俗名
senses.example: Every mining camp has a story about a sack of fool's gold.
senses.exampleCN: 每个矿营都有一个关于一袋愚人金的故事。
senses.why: The nickname carries the disappointment inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个绰号把失望装在里面。

senses.title: Its chemistry
senses.definition: iron sulphide, written as FeS2
senses.definitionCN: 硫化铁，写作 FeS2
senses.example: Pyrite is iron sulphide, not an ore of gold.
senses.exampleCN: 黄铁矿是硫化铁，不是金的矿石。
senses.why: The formula is the fact that ends the illusion.
senses.whyCN: 化学式就是终结幻觉的那个事实。

senses.title: Industrial use
senses.definition: a source of sulphur for making sulphuric acid
senses.definitionCN: 制造硫酸的硫来源
senses.example: The plant burned pyrite to produce sulphuric acid.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂焙烧黄铁矿来生产硫酸。
senses.why: Here the worthless-looking stone becomes useful.
senses.whyCN: 在这里，看似无价值的石头变得有用。

senses.title: In collections
senses.definition: a specimen valued for its bright cubic crystals
senses.definitionCN: 因其明亮立方晶体而受重视的标本
senses.example: The museum's pyrite specimen draws more photographers than geologists.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆那块黄铁矿标本吸引的摄影师比地质学家还多。
senses.why: Beauty and value are not the same thing.
senses.whyCN: 美与价值并不是一回事。

senses.title: Against real gold
senses.definition: harder and lighter than gold, and it tarnishes
senses.definitionCN: 比金更硬更轻，而且会失去光泽
senses.example: Real gold bends; pyrite cracks under the same hammer.
senses.exampleCN: 真金会弯，黄铁矿在同一把锤子下会裂。
senses.why: The practical tests are hardness and weight.
senses.whyCN: 实用的检验是硬度与重量。

senses.title: As a metaphor
senses.definition: any showy thing mistaken for something valuable
senses.definitionCN: 被误认为有价值之物的任何浮华东西
senses.example: The scheme had the shine of innovation and the substance of pyrite.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案有创新的光泽，实质却是黄铁矿。
senses.why: The mineral becomes a ready-made image for counterfeit promise.
senses.whyCN: 这种矿物成了现成的「虚假承诺」意象。

senses.title: The name from fire
senses.definition: the Greek name because it sparks when struck
senses.definitionCN: 因敲击时会迸出火花而得希腊名
senses.example: Strike pyrite against steel and you will see why it was named for fire.
senses.exampleCN: 把黄铁矿敲在钢上，你就明白它为何以火得名。
senses.why: The etymology restores the stone's original trick.
senses.whyCN: 词源恢复了这块石头最初的把戏。

intro.en: Pyrite comes from Greek pyr, 'fire', through pyrites lithos, the fire-stone that sparks when struck.
intro.cn: pyrite 经希腊语 pyrites lithos（火石）来自 pyr（火），因为敲击时会迸出火花。

items.en: Pyr was the ordinary Greek word for fire.
items.cn: pyr 是希腊语里普通的「火」字。

items.en: Pyrites lithos meant the stone that strikes fire.
items.cn: pyrites lithos 意为能击出火的石头。

items.en: Latin borrowed pyrites for a hard yellow mineral.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 pyrites，指一种坚硬的黄色矿物。

items.en: English shortened it to pyrite in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪把它缩略为 pyrite。

items.en: Miners added the name fool's gold from experience.
items.cn: 矿工凭经验加上了「愚人金」这个俗称。

note.en: The look-alike group plays on the pyre and pyr- roots; the near-meaning group separates fool's gold from its mineral relatives.
note.cn: 形近组玩的是 pyre 与 pyr 词根；近义组把「愚人金」与它的矿物亲属分开。

entries.definition: the plural and older mineral name.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，也是较早的矿物名。

entries.definition: a pile for burning a body.
entries.definitionCN: 焚烧尸体的柴堆。

entries.definition: an instrument for high temperatures.
entries.definitionCN: 测量高温的仪器。

entries.definition: relating to fireworks.
entries.definitionCN: 与烟火有关的。

entries.definition: any mineral mistaken for gold.
entries.definitionCN: 任何被误认为金的矿物。

entries.definition: a related iron sulphide mineral.
entries.definitionCN: 一种相关的硫化铁矿物。

entries.definition: a copper iron sulphide ore.
entries.definitionCN: 一种铜铁硫化物矿石。

entries.definition: rock from which metal can be extracted.
entries.definitionCN: 可从中提炼金属的岩石。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a glittering stone that cracks under a hammer.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一块闪光石头在锤下裂开」的画面。

normal.en: Pyrite begins with pyr, Greek for fire: strike it and it sparks.
normal.cn: pyrite 以 pyr 开头，希腊语的「火」：敲它就迸火花。

normal.en: Picture a prospector dancing, then a hammer ending the dance.
normal.cn: 想象淘金者先跳舞，然后一把锤子结束这支舞。

normal.en: Say PY-rite; it rhymes with bright, which is exactly the trap.
normal.cn: 读 PY-rite，与 bright 押韵，这正是陷阱所在。

normal.en: The plural pyrites also names a whole family of sulphides.
normal.cn: 复数 pyrites 也指整个硫化物家族。

normal.en: Gold bends, pyrite cracks: remember the hammer, not the shine.
normal.cn: 金会弯，黄铁矿会裂：记住锤子，不要记住光。

abstract.en: Pyrite is a lesson in valuation: the eye is a poor assay office.
abstract.cn: pyrite 是一堂估值课：眼睛是个糟糕的化验室。

abstract.en: The mineral is not a fraud; only the mistake about it is.
abstract.cn: 这种矿物本身不是骗局；骗局只在于对它的误判。

abstract.en: Every boom has its pyrite, and every boom learns the hammer test late.
abstract.cn: 每轮热潮都有自己的黄铁矿，而每轮热潮都太晚才学会锤子检验。

examples.en: The prospector thought he had struck gold, but the glitter was only pyrite.
examples.cn: 淘金者以为自己发现了金矿，但那点闪光只是黄铁矿。

examples.en: Pyrite is iron sulphide, not an ore of gold.
examples.cn: 黄铁矿是硫化铁，不是金的矿石。

examples.en: The scheme had the shine of innovation and the substance of pyrite.
examples.cn: 这个方案有创新的光泽，实质却是黄铁矿。

dict_mnemonic.text: pyr（火）+ ite（矿物后缀）→ 敲击迸火的石头，黄铁矿。

root: 希腊语 pyr（火）+ 矿物后缀 -ite

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses move from the mineral itself to its nickname, chemistry, industry, collections, the test against gold, the metaphor and the fiery name.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从矿物本身走到它的绰号、化学成分、工业、收藏、与真金的检验、比喻，以及那个带火的名字。

core.en: A GLITTER THAT CRACKS
core.cn: 一敲就裂的闪光

branches.en: The mineral and its formula.
branches.cn: 矿物本身与它的化学式。

branches.en: The nickname and the metaphor it feeds.
branches.cn: 绰号以及它喂养的比喻。

branches.en: Industrial sulphur.
branches.cn: 工业上的硫。

branches.en: Beauty kept in a case.
branches.cn: 被收进陈列柜的美。

branches.en: The hammer test and the name from fire.
branches.cn: 锤子检验与来自火的名字。

intro.en: The pyr- family is about fire: pyrite, pyre, pyrometer and pyrotechnic all carry it.
intro.cn: pyr 词族关乎火：pyrite、pyre、pyrometer、pyrotechnic 都带着它。

latinIntro.en: Greek pyr goes through Latin as pyrites; the mineral suffix -ite was added later by scientific naming.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 pyr 经拉丁语作 pyrites；矿物后缀 -ite 是后来科学命名加上去的。

definition_zh: v. 驳斥，反驳；对…提出异议
definition_en: to argue against a claim and deny it
core_image: 一支笔把纸上的结论划上一道横线
scene: 他逐条驳斥了报告里的说法。 He controverted each claim in the report.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：controvert 指驳斥；句意是他逐条反驳报告中的说法。

pos.zh: 驳斥；质疑

senses.title: Argue against
senses.definition: to argue that a claim is wrong
senses.definitionCN: 论证某说法是错的
senses.example: He controverted every claim.
senses.exampleCN: 他驳斥了每一条说法。
senses.why: A line drawn through a conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 在结论上划出的一道横线。

senses.title: Deny as false
senses.definition: to deny that something is true
senses.definitionCN: 否认某事为真
senses.example: She controverted the official story.
senses.exampleCN: 她否认了官方说法。
senses.why: A head shaken at a printed page.
senses.whyCN: 对着印好的页面摇头。

senses.title: Question in debate
senses.definition: to dispute something in formal debate
senses.definitionCN: 在正式辩论中提出异议
senses.example: The motion was controverted at length.
senses.exampleCN: 该动议被长时间质疑。
senses.why: Two sides pulling one statement apart.
senses.whyCN: 两方扯开同一句话。

intro.cn: controvert 把拉丁语 contra（反对）接到 vertere（转）上。

items.en: Vertere means to turn.
items.cn: vertere 意为转动。

items.en: Controvertere means to turn against.
items.cn: controvertere 意为转过来相对。

items.en: Controversia means a disputed matter.
items.cn: controversia 意为有争议之事。

items.en: It narrowed to arguing a claim down.
items.cn: 十七世纪收窄为驳倒某个说法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the controvert- family; the near-meaning group names refuting.
note.cn: 形近组属于同一 controvert- 词族；近义组都是「反驳」。

entries.definition: Public disagreement.
entries.definitionCN: 争议。

entries.definition: Causing disagreement.
entries.definitionCN: 有争议的。

entries.definition: To change into something else.
entries.definitionCN: 转换。

entries.definition: To prove a claim false.
entries.definitionCN: 驳倒。

entries.definition: To reply with a counter-argument.
entries.definitionCN: 反驳。

entries.definition: To argue that something is wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 质疑。

entries.definition: To state the opposite.

normalIntro.cn: controvert 把说法转过来正面顶上去。

normal.en: To controvert is to turn against a claim.

normal.en: A controverted point is one under attack.

normal.en: Controversy is the argument it starts.

abstract.en: A line struck through a conclusion.
abstract.cn: 被划掉的结论。

abstract.en: Two arrows pointing at each other.

abstract.en: A page turned around to face you.

examples.en: She controverted the report point by point.
examples.cn: 她逐点驳斥了那份报告。

examples.en: Nobody dared controvert the general.
examples.cn: 没人敢反驳这位将军。

examples.en: The claim was quickly controverted.
examples.cn: 那条说法很快被驳斥。

sensesIntro.en: Turning a claim around and striking it down.
sensesIntro.cn: 把说法转过来再打下去。

core.cn: 核心意象：被转过来正面迎击的说法

branches.en: A conclusion crossed out.
branches.cn: 被划掉的结论。

branches.en: An official story denied.

definition_zh: 感觉；知觉；轰动（事件或人）
definition_en: a physical feeling produced by the senses, or a state of great public excitement caused by something
core_image: 外界刺激撞上神经，在身体里亮起一阵可感的反应，随后传遍整群人
scene: 喝下冰水后，牙齿深处突然一阵尖锐的凉意，让人停住： A sharp sensation ran through her teeth as she bit into the ice.
sceneCN: 这里指「身体感觉」（第 1 个义项：由感官刺激产生的身体感受）；句意为她咬到冰块时，一阵尖锐的凉意穿过牙齿。

pos.zh: 感觉；知觉（身体上的感受）
轰动；引起轰动的人或事

derivatives.zh: 引起轰动的；耸人听闻的
耸人听闻的做法；感觉主义

senses.title: A physical feeling
senses.titleCN: 身体感觉：由刺激产生的一阵感受
senses.definition: a feeling in the body produced by something acting on the senses or on the nerves
senses.definitionCN: 由作用于感官或神经的刺激在身体中产生的感受
senses.example: A sharp sensation ran through her teeth as she bit into the ice.
senses.exampleCN: 她咬到冰块时，一阵尖锐的凉意穿过牙齿。
senses.why: The word names what is felt rather than what is sensed: the stimulus is outside, and the sensation is the body's response.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名「被感受到的东西」而非「被感知的对象」：刺激在外，感觉是身体的回应。

senses.title: Sensation and perception
senses.titleCN: 感觉（与知觉相对的概念）
senses.definition: the raw impression received by the senses, as studied in psychology before interpretation
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中未经解释、由感官接收的原始印象
senses.example: Psychology separates sensation from perception, the meaning given to it.
senses.exampleCN: 心理学把感觉与赋予其意义的知觉区分开来。
senses.why: In this technical pair, sensation is the input before the mind labels it, which is why the two words are always taught together.
senses.whyCN: 在这一技术配对中，「感觉」是心智贴标签之前的输入，因此两个词总是成对讲授。

senses.title: A public stir
senses.titleCN: 轰动：引起众人关注的事件
senses.definition: a sudden wave of public excitement or surprise caused by an event, a person or a work
senses.definitionCN: 由事件、人物或作品引起的突然而广泛的公众激动或惊讶
senses.example: The young pianist caused a sensation at her first concert.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻钢琴家在她的首场音乐会上引起轰动。
senses.why: The bodily meaning is transferred to a crowd: excitement runs through people the way a feeling runs through nerves.
senses.whyCN: 身体义被转用到人群：激动穿过众人，正如感觉穿过神经。

senses.title: A hit or a wonder
senses.definition: a person or work that becomes suddenly and widely famous
senses.definitionCN: 突然广为人知、红极一时的人或作品
senses.example: The novel was the sensation of the season.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说是当季最轰动的话题。
senses.why: The cause and the effect change places: the thing that produces the stir comes to be called the sensation itself.
senses.whyCN: 因果位置互换：引起轰动的事物本身也被称为「轰动」。

senses.title: Loss of sensation
senses.titleCN: 感觉丧失：身体某处不再有感受
senses.definition: the condition in which a part of the body can no longer feel touch, heat or pain
senses.definitionCN: 身体某部位不再能感受触、热或痛的状态
senses.example: Loss of sensation in the fingers can be a sign of nerve damage.
senses.exampleCN: 手指失去感觉可能是神经受损的迹象。
senses.why: The absence is defined against the presence: what is missing is exactly the feeling the word normally names.
senses.whyCN: 缺失是相对存在来定义的：失去的正是这个词通常所指的那种感受。

senses.title: Tactile sensation
senses.definition: the feeling produced when something touches or presses on the skin
senses.definitionCN: 某物接触或压迫皮肤时产生的感受
senses.example: Tactile sensation tells the hand how rough the stone is.
senses.exampleCN: 触觉告诉手这块石头有多粗糙。
senses.why: Each sense contributes its own kind of sensation, so the word is often paired with the channel that produced it.
senses.whyCN: 每种感官贡献自己的一类感觉，因此这个词常与产生它的通道搭配。

senses.title: Physiological reception
senses.titleCN: 生理学意义上的感觉接收
senses.definition: the process by which a receptor turns a stimulus into a nerve signal
senses.definitionCN: 感受器把刺激转成神经信号的过程
senses.example: The study measured sensation at the level of single receptors.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究在单个感受器层面测量感觉。
senses.why: At this level sensation is not yet a conscious feeling but the event of conversion that makes feeling possible.
senses.whyCN: 在这一层面，感觉还不是意识到的感受，而是使感受成为可能的转换事件。

senses.title: A feeling of unease
senses.titleCN: 某种抽象感受（不安、沉重）
senses.definition: a vague emotional or bodily impression, such as a sensation of dread or of weight
senses.definitionCN: 模糊的情绪或身体印象，如不安或沉重之感
senses.example: He woke with a sensation of dread he could not explain.
senses.exampleCN: 他醒来时有一种说不出的不安感。
senses.why: The word extends from concrete feeling to any impression that seems to arrive from outside the will.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从具体感受扩展到一切仿佛不请自来的印象。

intro.en: Sensation comes from Late Latin sensatio, built on sensus, the past participle of sentire to feel, and came into English through French. The public-stir sense is later. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: sensation 来自晚期拉丁 sensatio，建立在 sensus（sentire「感觉」的过去分词）之上，经法语进入英语。轰动义出现较晚。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sentire meant to feel or perceive, and sensus named the feeling that results.
items.cn: sentire 意为感觉或感知，sensus 指由此产生的感受。

items.en: Late Latin sensatio named the act or state of feeling; the suffix -tio marks a process or its result.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 sensatio 指感觉的动作或状态；后缀 -tio 标记过程或其结果。

items.en: French sensation carried the word into English in the seventeenth century, first in medical and philosophical writing.
items.cn: 法语 sensation 在 17 世纪把这个词带入英语，最初见于医学与哲学写作。

items.en: Eighteenth- and nineteenth-century psychology fixed the pair sensation and perception as separate stages.
items.cn: 18 至 19 世纪心理学把 sensation 与 perception 固定为两个不同阶段。

items.en: The sense of a public sensation developed in the eighteenth century, when newspapers began to report events as waves of excitement.
items.cn: 指公众轰动的义项在 18 世纪发展起来，当时报纸开始把事件报道为一阵阵激动。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the first English use of sensation is not firmly dated, and the exact point at which the public sense separated from the medical one is unclear.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：sensation 最早的英语书证没有确切年代，公众义从医学义中分出的确切时点也不清楚。

note.en: The first group holds same-root nouns and adjectives that are easily confused; the second holds words for related experiences.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、易混的名词与形容词；第二组是表示相近体验的词。

entries.definition: The general faculty of feeling or the meaning of a word; sensation is one specific feeling produced through it.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指感觉能力或词义；sensation 是通过它产生的一次具体感受。

entries.definition: Relating to the senses; it describes the channel, while sensation names what passes through it.
entries.definitionCN: 与感官有关的；它描述通道，而 sensation 命名通过通道的东西。

entries.definition: Causing or intended to cause a stir; it is the adjective of the public sense, not of bodily feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 引起或意图引起轰动的；它是公众义的形容词，而非身体感觉的形容词。

entries.definition: A view shaped by emotion; it also comes from sentire, but through a different Latin noun, and it means opinion or feeling rather than bodily sensation.
entries.definitionCN: 受情感影响的看法；同出 sentire，但经另一个拉丁名词，意为看法或情感，而非身体感受。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for any bodily or emotional experience; sensation is its more technical or vivid counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何身体或情绪体验的日常词；sensation 是更技术或更鲜明的对应词。

entries.definition: The meaning the mind gives to what the senses deliver; sensation is the raw impression before that meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 心智赋予感官内容的意义；sensation 是意义之前的原始印象。

entries.definition: A general effect left on the mind or senses; it is vaguer and less physical than sensation.
entries.definitionCN: 留在心智或感官上的一般印象；比 sensation 更模糊、更少身体性。

entries.definition: A sudden wave of excitement; it is close to the public sense of sensation but always pleasurable.
entries.definitionCN: 突然的一阵兴奋；接近 sensation 的公众义，但总带有愉悦。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin process noun, the real psychology pair and the real newspaper phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁过程名词、真实的心理学配对与真实的报纸短语。

normal.en: Sensus is feeling, and -atio marks a process, so sensation is the event of feeling something.
normal.cn: sensus 是感觉，-atio 标记过程，因此 sensation 是「感觉到某物」这一事件。

normal.en: Psychology teaches sensation first and perception second: raw input, then meaning.
normal.cn: 心理学先讲 sensation 后讲 perception：先原始输入，后意义。

normal.en: Cause a sensation is the fixed newspaper phrase for a public stir.
normal.cn: cause a sensation 是报纸上表示「引起轰动」的固定说法。

normal.en: Loss of sensation is the clinical phrase for numbness or nerve damage.
normal.cn: loss of sensation 是表示麻木或神经损伤的临床说法。

normal.en: The adjective splits in two: sensory for the channel, sensational for the stir.
normal.cn: 形容词分成两条：sensory 指通道，sensational 指轰动。

abstract.en: Picture a struck bell: the blow is outside, the ring is inside the body.
abstract.cn: 想象一口被敲响的钟：敲击在外，余音在身体里。

abstract.en: Picture a wave crossing a crowd: one person feels it, then everyone feels it.
abstract.cn: 想象一阵波穿过人群：先是一个人感到，然后所有人都感到。

abstract.en: Picture a switch that can also be off: numbness is the same circuit with no current.
abstract.cn: 想象一个也能关闭的开关：麻木就是同一条电路断了电流。

examples.en: A burning sensation in the chest should be checked by a doctor.
examples.cn: 胸部灼热感应当请医生检查。

examples.en: The invention caused a sensation at the 1900 world fair.
examples.cn: 这项发明在 1900 年世界博览会上引起轰动。

examples.en: The drug reduces sensation in the skin before surgery.
examples.cn: 这种药在手术前降低皮肤的感觉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「三筛神」（sensation）——三层筛选后，神经感到的那一下 → 感觉；轰动

root: 晚期拉丁 sensatio「感觉（过程或状态）」，来自 sensus（sentire「感觉、感知」的过去分词）；经法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a single bodily feeling to the psychological concept, then out into public excitement, a famous work, numbness, touch, receptor-level reception, and finally a vague impression of dread.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一次身体感受出发，到心理学概念，再走向公众轰动、成名作品、麻木、触觉、感受器层面的接收，最后是模糊的不安印象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stimulus strikes a nerve and a felt response lights up inside the body.
core.cn: 核心意象：刺激撞上神经，身体内部亮起一阵可感的回应。

branches.en: LOSS AND TOUCH: feeling can vanish, and one channel still delivers it.
branches.cn: 丧失与触觉：感觉会消失，而某个通道仍能传递它。

branches.en: THE TECHNICAL LADDER: the psychological input and the receptor event beneath it.
branches.cn: 技术阶梯：心理学的输入概念，以及其下感受器层面的事件。

branches.en: THE WONDER: the thing itself becomes famous overnight.
branches.cn: 轰动之物：那件事物本身一夜之间人尽皆知。

branches.en: VAGUE IMPRESSION: a feeling that arrives without a clear source.
branches.cn: 模糊印象：没有明确来源却出现的感受。

branches.en: ONE METAPHOR, TWO SCALES: nerves and crowds both conduct a wave of feeling.
branches.cn: 一个比喻两种尺度：神经与人群都在传导一阵感受。

intro.en: Sensation is a Latin process noun: the stem sens- plus -ation, the English form of Latin -tio.
intro.cn: sensation 是拉丁过程名词：词干 sens- 加 -ation，即拉丁 -tio 的英语形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin sentire gives sensus and sensatio; the adjective sensualis and the noun sentimentum belong to neighbouring branches of the same family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sentire 衍生 sensus 与 sensatio；形容词 sensualis 与名词 sentimentum 属于同一词族的邻近支线。

items.example: The whole family rests on this verb.
items.exampleCN: 整个词族都建立在这个动词上。

items.example: Sensus is the noun behind sense.
items.exampleCN: sensus 是 sense 背后的名词。

items.example: The suffix turns a verb into a noun of process.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成过程名词。

items.example: A sharp sensation ran through her teeth.
items.exampleCN: 一阵尖锐的感觉穿过她的牙齿。

items.example: Sensory nerves carry the signal inward.
items.exampleCN: 感觉神经把信号向体内传导。

items.example: The paper was accused of sensationalism.
items.exampleCN: 这家报纸被指刻意耸人听闻。

items.meaning: able to be felt; also reasonable
items.exampleCN: 这点差别几乎感觉不到。

items.example: The scarred skin was insensitive to touch.
items.exampleCN: 留疤的皮肤对触摸不敏感。

definition_zh: 迁移模式；迁徙规律
definition_en: the regular route, direction and timing along which people or animals move
core_image: 一张地图上画着几条同向箭头，每年在同一季节出现，线路几乎不变
scene: 这里指「迁移模式」。 Satellite tags revealed a migration pattern that crosses three countries.
sceneCN: 这里 migration pattern 指「迁徙的固定路线与时间规律」（第 2 个义项：动物逐年沿同一路径移动的规律）；句意为卫星标签揭示出一条横跨三国的迁徙模式。图中可辨识物件：同向箭头、季节标记、国界线、卫星轨迹点。

pos.zh: 迁移模式；迁徙规律（可数，复数 migration patterns）

senses.title: A regular route for people
senses.definition: the repeated direction and timing of people moving from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 人们从一地迁往另一地时重复出现的方向与时间
senses.example: The census records the migration pattern from farm to factory town.
senses.exampleCN: 人口普查记录了从农场到工厂镇的迁移模式。
senses.why: migration names the movement and pattern names its repeated shape, so the phrase describes movement that is not random.
senses.whyCN: migration 命名移动，pattern 命名其重复的形状，因此这个短语描述的是非随机的移动。

senses.title: A seasonal animal route
senses.titleCN: 动物的季节性迁徙规律
senses.definition: the yearly route and timing followed by animals between breeding and wintering grounds
senses.definitionCN: 动物在繁殖地与越冬地之间逐年遵循的路线与时间
senses.example: Satellite tags revealed a migration pattern that crosses three countries.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星标签揭示出一条横跨三国的迁徙模式。
senses.why: because animals repeat the same path each year, their movement is the clearest case of a pattern.
senses.whyCN: 动物每年重复同一条路，因此它们的移动是最典型的「模式」。

senses.title: A rural-urban flow
senses.definition: the movement of people from countryside to cities, often in stages
senses.definitionCN: 人口由乡村流向城市、常分阶段进行的移动
senses.example: The rural-urban migration pattern emptied the villages first and the towns later.
senses.exampleCN: 城乡迁移模式先抽空村庄，之后才轮到小镇。
senses.why: a direction that repeats across a whole society is a pattern, and the countryside-to-city flow is the classic one.
senses.whyCN: 在整个社会中重复出现的流向就是模式，而由乡到城的流动正是经典一例。

senses.title: Circular movement
senses.titleCN: 循环迁移模式：往返而不定居
senses.definition: repeated going and returning between two places without permanent settlement
senses.definitionCN: 在两处之间反复往返而不永久定居
senses.example: Seasonal work produced a circular migration pattern across the border.
senses.exampleCN: 季节性工作造成了跨境往返的循环迁移模式。
senses.why: when movement returns to its start, the pattern closes into a loop, which is why it is named separately.
senses.whyCN: 当移动回到起点，模式就闭合成一个环，因此它被单独命名。

senses.title: Movement in steps
senses.titleCN: 阶梯式迁移模式：逐级向城市靠近
senses.definition: movement toward a city in successive stages rather than one leap
senses.definitionCN: 分几个阶段逐步向城市靠近，而非一步到位
senses.example: The step migration pattern moved families to the county town before the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 阶梯式迁移模式让家庭先进县城，再进首都。
senses.why: family migration often proceeds by stages, so the staircase is a pattern in its own right.
senses.whyCN: 家庭迁移常分阶段推进，因此这种阶梯本身就是一种模式。

senses.title: A measurable series
senses.definition: the sequence of movements recorded over time and plotted as data
senses.definitionCN: 随时间记录并绘制成数据的移动序列
senses.example: The migration pattern data show a peak every October.
senses.exampleCN: 迁移模式数据显示每年十月出现峰值。
senses.why: once the route is counted year after year, it becomes a series with a shape that can be plotted.
senses.whyCN: 一旦路线被年复一年地计数，它就变成一条可绘出形状的序列。

senses.title: A bird flyway
senses.definition: the corridor along which a population of birds travels each year
senses.definitionCN: 某一鸟群每年行经的走廊地带
senses.example: The flyway is the migration pattern written on the map.
senses.exampleCN: 迁飞通道就是画在地图上的迁徙模式。
senses.why: geographers name the corridor, and the corridor is simply the pattern given a boundary.
senses.whyCN: 地理学者给走廊命名，而走廊不过是给模式画了边界。

senses.title: A route shifting with climate
senses.titleCN: 随气候变化而改变的路线
senses.definition: a route whose timing or direction changes as temperatures and seasons shift
senses.definitionCN: 随气温与季节变化而改变时间或方向的路线
senses.example: Warming seas have altered the migration pattern of the whales.
senses.exampleCN: 海水变暖改变了鲸的迁徙模式。
senses.why: a pattern held in place by climate can move when the climate moves, which is why the phrase pairs with changing.
senses.whyCN: 被气候固定的模式会随气候变化而移动，因此这个短语常与 changing 搭配。

intro.en: Migration comes from Latin migratio, from migrare 'to move'; pattern comes through Old French patron from Latin patronus 'protector'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: migration 来自拉丁 migratio，源于 migrare「移动」；pattern 经古法语 patron 来自拉丁 patronus「保护人」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Migrare meant 'to move from one place to another'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; a link to meare 'to go, pass' is a hypothesis, not an established derivation.
items.cn: migrare 意为「从一处迁往另一处」。其更深来源不确定；把它与 meare「行走、经过」联系只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Migratio named a removal or change of abode; English took migration in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: migratio 指迁居或更换住所；英语于 17 世纪吸收 migration。

items.en: Patronus meant 'protector, patron', from pater 'father'; Old French patron gained the sense of a model or example.
items.cn: patronus 意为「保护人、赞助人」，源自 pater「父亲」；古法语 patron 又获得「范本、样式」之义。

items.en: English pattern, from the same French word, first meant a model to copy and later a repeated arrangement.
items.cn: 英语 pattern 出自同一法语词，最初指供模仿的范本，后来指重复出现的排列。

items.en: The compound migration pattern became common in the twentieth century with bird banding and census mapping.
items.cn: 组合 migration pattern 在 20 世纪随鸟类环志与普查制图而普及。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest use of the exact phrase is not precisely recorded, and the origins of Latin migrare and of the 'model' sense of pattern both remain debated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这一确切短语的最早使用没有精确记录；拉丁 migrare 的来源与 pattern 的「范本」义来源都仍有争议。

note.en: Group one holds migration words that are easily mixed; group two holds terms for routes and repeated movement.
note.cn: 第一组是容易混淆的 migration 词族；第二组是路线与重复移动的相关词。

entries.definition: The act of moving; a migration pattern is the repeated shape that movement takes.
entries.definitionCN: 指移动本身；migration pattern 是这种移动反复呈现的形状。

entries.definition: Describes a species or person that migrates, as in migratory birds; it does not name the route.
entries.definitionCN: 描述会迁徙的物种或人，如候鸟；不命名路线。

entries.definition: A person or animal that moves; migrant workers are the human case of the same word.
entries.definitionCN: 指移动的人或动物；migrant workers 是这个词的人的例子。

entries.definition: E- 'out' plus migration: leaving a country, seen from the place left behind.
entries.definitionCN: e-「向外」加 migration：离开一国，从被离开之地的视角看。

entries.definition: The fixed corridor used by migrating birds; it is the geographic name for one kind of pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 指候鸟使用的固定走廊；是某一类模式在地理上的名称。

entries.definition: The path taken; a route can be travelled once, while a pattern implies repetition.
entries.definitionCN: 指所走的路径；路线可以只走一次，而模式含重复之意。

entries.definition: Any repeated shape of movement, from traffic to troops; it is not tied to long-distance relocation.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何重复的移动形状，从交通到部队；不限于长途迁居。

entries.definition: A general direction in which something is changing; a pattern may persist without any trend.
entries.definitionCN: 指某事物变化的大方向；模式可以持续存在而不构成趋势。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: migration 'moving' + pattern 'repeated shape': movement that repeats.
normal.cn: migration「移动」+ pattern「重复形状」：重复发生的移动。

normal.en: The family runs migrate, migration, migratory, migrant, pattern.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 migrate、migration、migratory、migrant、pattern。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: seasonal migration pattern, rural-urban migration pattern, circular migration pattern.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：季节性迁徙模式、城乡迁移模式、循环迁移模式。

normal.en: Bird banding and satellite tags are how such patterns are proved.
normal.cn: 鸟类环志与卫星标签是证实这类模式的手段。

normal.en: Pattern came from a word for a model to copy, which is why a route that repeats is a pattern.
normal.cn: pattern 出自「供模仿的范本」，因此重复的路线才叫模式。

abstract.en: Picture arrows on a map that reappear every autumn in the same places.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上的箭头每年秋天在同一处重新出现。

abstract.en: Picture a river of birds following a line no one drew.
abstract.cn: 想象一条鸟的河流沿着无人画过的线走。

abstract.en: Picture a family moving one town closer each decade.
abstract.cn: 想象一家人每十年往城市靠近一镇。

examples.en: The migration pattern of the geese follows four river valleys.
examples.cn: 这些雁的迁徙模式沿四条河谷展开。

examples.en: Census data reveal a migration pattern toward the coast.
examples.cn: 普查数据揭示出向沿海迁移的模式。

examples.en: Dams can break a migration pattern built over centuries.
examples.cn: 水坝能打断延续数百年的迁徙模式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「migration（迁移）+ pattern（图案）」——每年在同一张图上画同样的箭头 → 迁移模式

root: 拉丁 migrare「迁移」（更深来源不确定）+ migratio「迁居」；pattern 经古法语 patron 来自拉丁 patronus「保护人」（源自 pater「父亲」），后引申为「范本、样式」。英语 migration pattern。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shape: movement repeats, and that repetition is then read as a human route, an animal season, a rural flow, a loop, a staircase, a data series, a flyway and a route that is now shifting.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个形状展开：移动反复发生，这个重复再被读成人的路线、动物的季节、乡村流向、环线、阶梯、数据序列、迁飞通道，以及正在改变的路线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: arrows that reappear in the same places every season.
core.cn: 核心意象：每个季节都在同一处重新出现的箭头。

branches.en: HUMAN ROUTES: farm to city, and the stages in between.
branches.cn: 人的路线：从乡村到城市，以及其间的阶段。

branches.en: ANIMAL SEASONS: the same shape drawn as a flyway on a map.
branches.cn: 动物的季节：同一形状在地图上画成迁飞通道。

branches.en: LOOPS AND STAIRS: movement without settlement, and movement in steps.
branches.cn: 环线与阶梯：不定居的往返，与分步靠近。

branches.en: DATA SERIES: the pattern becomes a curve with peaks.
branches.cn: 数据序列：模式变成带峰值的曲线。

branches.en: SHIFTING SHAPE: warming seas redraw the same arrows.
branches.cn: 变化的形状：海水变暖把同样的箭头重画。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin-derived noun of moving to an English noun of repeated shape that came through French from a word for a patron.
intro.cn: 这个短语把源自拉丁的「移动」名词，接到一个表示「重复形状」的英语名词上，后者经法语来自表示「保护人」的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin migrare gives migrate, migration, migratory and migrant; Latin patronus gives patron, pattern and patronize.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 migrare 衍生 migrate、migration、migratory 与 migrant；拉丁 patronus 衍生 patron、pattern 与 patronize。

items.structure: migrare, migravi, migratum (Latin verb, first conjugation)
items.example: The root supplies the movement itself.

items.meaning: a moving from place to place

items.example: The birds migrate along the coast.
The marsh is a stop for migratory birds.
items.exampleCN: 这片沼泽是候鸟的停歇地。

items.example: The Latin noun named a protector.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词指保护人。

items.example: Satellite tags revealed the migration pattern.

向外移民使这座岛空了。

definition_zh: 扩大；增高（权力、地位）；抬高（自己）
definition_en: to increase the power, wealth, or rank of; to make oneself seem greater
core_image: 权力雪球：有人不断往自己的权杖上加码
scene: 总裁把同盟的部门逐一吞并，权柄日益膨胀。 The CEO aggrandized his own office by absorbing every allied department.
sceneCN: 这里 aggrandize 是「扩大、增高（权力地位）」（第 2 个义项：使权力或地位增大）；句意是总裁通过吞并盟友部门来不断扩充自己的职权。

pos.zh: 扩大；增高（权力、财富、地位）

derivatives.zh: aggrandize 加名词后缀 -ment，义为「扩大；（权力、地位的）增高」
同根形容词，义为「宏大的；雄伟的」
grand 的名词形式，义为「壮丽；高贵」
同根地质学术语，义为「（河流）加积、淤高」

senses.title: To make oneself seem or become greater
senses.definition: to give oneself more importance, often at others' expense
senses.definitionCN: 给自己增加重要性，常以牺牲他人为代价
senses.example: He tells war stories only to aggrandize himself before new hires.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲从前的光辉事迹，只为在新人面前抬高自己。
senses.why: The root grand means great; when the arrow of making-great turns back on the doer, self-importance is the result.
senses.whyCN: 词根 grand 意为「大」；当「使之变大」的箭头折回施动者自身，便长出「自我抬高」之义。

senses.title: To increase the power, wealth, or territory of a person or state
senses.definition: to enlarge the scope of someone's authority, riches, or dominion
senses.definitionCN: 扩大某人的职权、财富或统治范围
senses.example: The CEO aggrandized his own office by absorbing every allied department.
senses.exampleCN: 总裁通过吞并所有盟友部门来不断扩充自己的职权。
senses.why: This is the historical core: crowns and estates grew the way a snowball does, by adding everything nearby.
senses.whyCN: 这是词义的历史核心：王权与领地像雪球一样，靠不断吞并周围的一切而增大。

intro.en: From French agrandir, built on grand (great), remodelled with the Latin-looking ending -ize in English.
intro.cn: 源自法语 agrandir（使变大），建立在 grand（大）之上；英语中又按拉丁词形改写成 -ize 结尾。

items.en: grandis meant great, large; it gave Old French grand.
items.cn: 拉丁语 grandis 意为「大的、宏伟的」，派生古法语 grand。

items.en: agrandir meant to make greater, to enlarge.
items.cn: 古法语 agrandir 意为「使变大；扩大」。

items.en: Borrowed as aggradeise and reshaped to aggrandize with the productive -ize ending.
items.cn: 十六世纪借入英语，初作 aggradeise，后依 -ize 后缀改写为 aggrandize。

items.en: Applied to crowns, estates, and offices; the reflexive self-aggrandizing use grew alongside.
items.cn: 用于王权、地产与官职；「自我膨胀」的反身用法随之发展。

items.en: Now often pejorative: self-aggrandizement names vain self-promotion.
items.cn: 如今常带贬义：self-aggrandizement 指虚荣的自我抬举。

note.en: Aggrandize belongs to the grand family; its near neighbours all describe enlargement, but with different materials.
note.cn: aggrandize 属 grand 词族；近邻词都表「扩大」，但扩张的对象各异。

entries.definition: large and impressive
entries.definitionCN: 宏大的；壮丽的——词根本尊

entries.definition: pretentiously grand
entries.definitionCN: 浮夸的；华而不实的——同根贬义分支

entries.definition: to make worse
entries.definitionCN: 使恶化；激怒——词首 ag- 相似，词根不同（gravis，重）

entries.definition: impressive greatness
entries.definitionCN: 壮丽；高贵——grand 的名词形式

entries.definition: to make something appear larger
entries.definitionCN: 放大；夸大——多指视觉或程度

entries.definition: to raise in rank or praise highly
entries.definitionCN: 擢升；颂扬——强调地位与荣誉

entries.definition: to spread out or increase in size
entries.definitionCN: 扩展——中性词，无自利色彩

entries.definition: to make someone seem unimportant
entries.definitionCN: 贬低；轻视——aggrandize 的反义

normalIntro.en: See grand inside the word: ag- + grand + -ize means to make grand.
normalIntro.cn: 在词里看见 grand：ag- + grand + -ize ＝「使变大」。

normal.en: ag + grand + ize: make someone grand
normal.cn: ag+grand+ize：让某人变得「宏大」

normal.en: self-aggrandizing is the common critical phrase
normal.cn: self-aggrandizing 是常见的批评用语：自我膨胀的

normal.en: grandeur, grandiose, aggrandize: one family of greatness
normal.cn: grandeur、grandiose、aggrandize 同属「大」的家族

normal.en: aggravate looks close but means make worse, not greater
normal.cn: aggravate 拼写相近但义为「恶化」，不是「扩大」

normal.en: aggrandize one's power: snowball the authority
normal.cn: aggrandize one's power：像滚雪球一样累积权柄

abstract.en: A throne gathering cushions until it towers over the hall
abstract.cn: 王座不断垫高，直至俯瞰整个大厅

abstract.en: A man standing on borrowed coats to look taller
abstract.cn: 一个人踩着借来的外衣，只为显得更高

abstract.en: A map where one color keeps swallowing its neighbours
abstract.cn: 地图上一种颜色不断吞并邻居的疆土

examples.en: Critics said the monument was built purely to aggrandize the dictator.
examples.cn: 批评者说，那座纪念碑纯粹是为了给独裁者抬轿撑场面。

examples.en: The dynasty aggrandized its realm through three centuries of treaties and wars.
examples.cn: 这个王朝通过三个世纪的条约与战争不断扩张版图。

examples.en: His memoir is honest, never seeking to aggrandize its author.
examples.cn: 他的回忆录写得坦诚，从未试图拔高作者自己。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿哥抓的（权）」——阿哥抓的权越来越大，自我膨胀。谐音仅助记，并非词源。

root: 拉丁语 grandis（大）经古法语 agrandir「使大」进入英语，前缀 ag-（ad-，朝向）加强方向；「使之变大」先指王权财富的扩张，后折回自身成为「自我抬高」。

sensesIntro.en: One verb of enlarging splits by target: outward dominion or the speaker's own image.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「增大」动词按对象分岔：对外的权势扩张，或对内的自我抬举。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a snowball of power growing by absorbing neighbours
core.cn: 核心意象：靠吞并邻居越滚越大的权力雪球

branches.en: thrones and estates grown by addition
branches.cn: 靠兼并增大的王权与领地

branches.en: offices absorbing allied departments
branches.cn: 职权吞并盟友部门

branches.en: one verb of enlargement, two targets
branches.cn: 同一个扩大动词，两种对象

branches.en: turning the enlargement inward
branches.cn: 把「变大」的箭头折向自身

branches.en: importance claimed without merit
branches.cn: 没有实绩却自抬身价

intro.en: The word combines the prefix ag- (ad-) with the grand root and the verbal suffix -ize.
intro.cn: 该词由前缀 ag-（即 ad-）、词根 grand 与动词后缀 -ize 组合而成。

latinIntro.en: The grand root family is large and mostly neutral to pejorative.
latinIntro.cn: grand 词族规模不小，感情色彩从中性到贬义不等。

items.exampleCN: aggrandize、aggravate 中 g 前的 ad- 均写作 ag-

latinEntries.exampleCN: grand 与 aggrandize 的共同词根

definition_zh: n. 眩晕；头晕；头昏眼花；眼花缭乱的忙乱
definition_en: the feeling that everything is spinning and that you may fall, or a confused whirl of activity
core_image: 一个缓缓倾斜的房间，一只手抓住门框；空桌上一个空盘子旁边放着一杯水；一架梯子顶端映着下方很远的地面；一张被电话和成摞文件夹埋住的桌子
scene: 她刚站起来，整间屋子就慢慢倾斜了，一只手赶紧抓住门框。 A wave of dizziness made her sit down.
sceneCN: 这里 dizziness 是「眩晕」（第 1 个义项：觉得自己或房间在旋转）；句意：一阵眩晕让她坐了下来。图中可辨识物件：倾斜的房间、门框、抓住门框的手、椅子。

pos.zh: 眩晕；头晕；头昏眼花；眼花缭乱的忙乱

senses.title: The room spins
senses.definition: the feeling that you or the room is turning round
senses.definitionCN: （名词）觉得自己或房间在旋转的感觉
senses.example: A wave of dizziness made her sit down.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵眩晕让她坐了下来。
senses.why: A room tilting slowly while a hand grips the door frame.
senses.whyCN: 一个缓缓倾斜的房间，一只手抓住门框。

senses.title: Faint and unsteady
senses.definition: a weak, unsteady feeling from illness or lack of food
senses.definitionCN: （名词）因病或没吃东西而产生的发虚、站不稳的感觉
senses.example: He complained of dizziness after skipping lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 他没吃午饭后抱怨头晕。
senses.why: An empty plate beside a glass of water on a bare table.
senses.whyCN: 空桌上一个空盘子旁边放着一杯水。

senses.title: Unsteadiness at height
senses.definition: the unsteady feeling brought on by looking down from a height
senses.definitionCN: （名词）从高处往下看时产生的站立不稳感
senses.example: The dizziness passed once she stepped back from the edge.
senses.exampleCN: 她从边缘退后一步，眩晕就过去了。
senses.why: A ladder top seen against the ground far below.
senses.whyCN: 一架梯子顶端映着下方很远的地面。

senses.title: A whirl of activity
senses.definition: a confused state caused by too much happening at once
senses.definitionCN: （名词）太多事情同时发生而造成的混乱状态
senses.example: The dizziness of the first week at work slowly faded.
senses.exampleCN: 上班第一周那种晕头转向慢慢消退了。
senses.why: A desk buried under ringing phones and stacked folders.
senses.whyCN: 一张被响个不停的电话和成摞文件夹埋住的桌子。

intro.en: Dizziness is dizzy plus -ness, the state of; dizzy began as Old English dysig, foolish, and only later came to mean giddy, so the noun once described a muddled head rather than a spinning room.
intro.cn: dizziness 由 dizzy 加 -ness「…的状态」构成；dizzy 起初是古英语 dysig「愚蠢」，后来才变成「头晕」，所以这个名词曾指糊涂的脑子，而非旋转的房间。

items.en: Old English dysig meant foolish or stupid.
items.cn: 古英语 dysig 意为愚蠢的。

items.en: Middle English dizy still meant foolish.
items.cn: 中古英语 dizy 仍意为愚蠢的。

items.en: The sense shifts from foolish to giddy.
items.cn: 词义从「愚蠢」转向「头晕」。

items.en: Dizziness is used for the spinning feeling itself.
items.cn: dizziness 被用来指旋转感本身。

items.en: The noun names a common symptom reported to doctors.
items.cn: 这个名词指病人向医生描述的一种常见症状。

note.en: Dizziness is the state of a spinning head; its look-alikes share the dizzy stem or the idea of being stunned, and its neighbours name related unsteady feelings.
note.cn: dizziness 是头脑旋转的状态；形近词共用 dizzy 词干或「发懵」的意思，近义词则是相关的站不稳的感觉。

entries.definition: feeling that things are spinning
entries.definitionCN: 觉得东西在旋转的

entries.definition: to blind someone briefly with bright light
entries.definitionCN: 用强光使人短暂目眩

entries.definition: a state of being unable to think clearly
entries.definitionCN: 无法清楚思考的状态

entries.definition: a feeling of spinning from height or illness
entries.definitionCN: 由高处或疾病引起的旋转感

entries.definition: a light, unsteady, almost happy feeling
entries.definitionCN: 轻飘、站不稳、近乎兴奋的感觉

entries.definition: a feeling of being about to faint
entries.definitionCN: 快要晕倒的感觉
