dict_mnemonic.text: dizziness ＝ dizzy（头晕的）＋ -ness（名词后缀，表示状态）＝「头晕的状态」。dizzy 在古英语里原本指「愚蠢」，后来才转成「站不稳、天旋地转」，所以这个词既管身体也管忙乱。

root: 古英语 dysig（愚蠢）→ 中古英语 dizy → 英语 dizzy ＋ -ness → dizziness

sensesIntro.en: One unsteady head in four scenes: a tilting room, an empty plate, a ladder top above far ground and a desk buried in ringing phones.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个稳不住的脑袋的四个场景：倾斜的房间、空盘子、远地面之上的梯子顶端与被电话埋住的桌子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room tilting slowly while a hand grips the door frame and an empty plate sits beside a glass of water
core.cn: 核心意象：一个缓缓倾斜的房间，一只手抓住门框，空盘子旁放着一杯水

branches.en: The room seems to turn round.
branches.cn: 房间似乎在旋转。

branches.en: The body is weak and unsteady.
branches.cn: 身体发虚、站不稳。

branches.en: Height makes the ground swim.
branches.cn: 高度让地面晃动起来。

branches.en: Too much at once muddles the mind.
branches.cn: 事情一齐涌来把脑子搅乱。

branches.en: Both are a spinning sensation in the head.
branches.cn: 两者都是头里的旋转感。

intro.en: Dizziness is dizzy plus -ness; the adverb adds -ily, while the Latin turn root vert- builds vertigo, a cousin in meaning.
intro.cn: dizziness 由 dizzy 加 -ness 构成；副词再加 -ily，而拉丁语「转」的词根 vert- 造出 vertigo，是意思上的表亲。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertere means to turn and vertigo a whirling; the English stem dizzy is native, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vertere 意为转，vertigo 意为旋转；英语 dizzy 这个词干是本族语，不是拉丁语。

definition_zh: 断层线；断层带在地表的位置；（比喻）分歧线、裂痕
definition_en: the line where a fault reaches the surface, or a figurative line of division
core_image: 地表上一条细长的裂缝，两边地面属于不同的岩块，裂缝沿线一字排开
scene: 地面上有一道细长的裂口，几个小镇沿着它分布。 A row of small towns sits along the fault line, where the ground is cracked.
sceneCN: 这里 fault line 指「断层线」（第 1 个义项：断层在地表出露的位置）；句意为几个小镇沿着这条地面裂开的断层线分布。

pos.zh: 断层线；断层带；比喻分歧线

senses.title: The surface trace of a fault
senses.titleCN: 断层线：断层在地表的出露位置
senses.definition: the line along which a fault intersects the Earth's surface
senses.definitionCN: 断层与地表相交的那条线
senses.example: A row of small towns sits along the fault line, where the ground is cracked.
senses.exampleCN: 几个小镇沿这条地面裂开的断层线分布。
senses.why: A fault is a surface in three dimensions; where it cuts the ground it appears as a line.
senses.whyCN: 断层是三维空间中的一个面；它切过地面时就表现为一条线。

senses.title: The fault zone
senses.definition: the belt of broken ground around a fault trace
senses.definitionCN: 断层迹线周围破碎地面构成的带
senses.example: Buildings inside the fault line were reinforced.
senses.exampleCN: 断层带内的建筑做了加固。
senses.why: In ordinary usage the line stands for the whole broken belt, because the damage is not confined to one metre.
senses.whyCN: 在日常用法中，这条线代表整个破碎带，因为破坏并不限于一米宽。

senses.title: A seismic line
senses.definition: a line along which earthquakes are expected because a fault is active
senses.definitionCN: 因断层活动而预期发生地震的线
senses.example: The map marks every active fault line in red.
senses.exampleCN: 地图用红色标出每一条活动断层线。
senses.why: Active faults release strain repeatedly, so planning maps treat their traces as hazard lines.
senses.whyCN: 活动断层反复释放应变，因此规划图把它们的迹线当作灾害线。

senses.title: The mapped trace
senses.definition: the line drawn on a geological map to represent a fault
senses.definitionCN: 地质图上用来表示断层的那条线
senses.example: The fault line on the map is dashed where its position is uncertain.
senses.exampleCN: 地图上的断层线在位置不确定处画成虚线。
senses.why: Mapping reduces a three-dimensional surface to a symbol, and the symbol is a line.
senses.whyCN: 填图把三维的面简化为符号，而这个符号就是一条线。

senses.title: A line of weakness in a material
senses.definition: a line along which a material is likely to break
senses.definitionCN: 材料容易沿之断裂的线
senses.example: The crack followed a fault line in the cast metal.
senses.exampleCN: 裂缝沿着铸金属中的一条薄弱线扩展。
senses.why: The engineering use borrows the geological image for any prepared path of failure.
senses.whyCN: 工程用法借用地质形象，指任何预设的破坏路径。

senses.title: A political division
senses.definition: a figurative line separating opposed groups or opinions
senses.definitionCN: 分隔对立群体或意见的比喻性界线
senses.example: The treaty drew a new political fault line across the region.
senses.exampleCN: 这项条约在该地区划出一条新的政治分歧线。
senses.why: Two sides that no longer align are like two blocks offset along a seam, so the metaphor is structural.
senses.whyCN: 两侧不再对齐，就像沿缝错开的两块岩体，所以这个比喻是结构性的。

senses.title: A social fracture
senses.definition: a deep division in a society that may suddenly widen
senses.definitionCN: 社会中可能突然扩大的深层分裂
senses.example: Housing costs exposed a fault line between generations.
senses.exampleCN: 住房成本暴露出代际之间的一条裂痕。
senses.why: The image predicts sudden rupture: a line that looks quiet can slip when stress builds.
senses.whyCN: 这个形象预示突然破裂：看似平静的线在应力积累时会错动。

senses.title: A dividing line within an organisation
senses.definition: a split between factions inside a group or alliance
senses.definitionCN: 群体或联盟内部派系之间的分裂
senses.example: The budget vote revealed a fault line in the coalition.
senses.exampleCN: 预算投票暴露出执政联盟内部的一条分界线。
senses.why: An alliance holds together like a rock mass, and a fault line is where it may separate.
senses.whyCN: 联盟像岩体一样连在一起，而断层线就是它可能分开的地方。

intro.en: Fault line is an English compound of the geological noun fault and the Latin-derived noun line, used both literally and as a metaphor. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: fault line 是英语复合词，由地质名词 fault 与拉丁来源的名词 line 构成，既有字面用法，也有比喻用法。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fault goes back to Latin fallere 'to fail, deceive' through Old French faute, and acquired its rock-break sense in mining.
items.cn: fault 经古法语 faute 上溯到拉丁语 fallere「失败、欺骗」，并在采矿用语中获得岩石破裂义。

items.en: Line comes from Latin linea 'string, cord, line', from linum 'flax', and already meant a drawn stroke in classical use.
items.cn: line 来自拉丁语 linea「绳、线」，再上溯到 linum「亚麻」，在古典用法中已指画出的线条。

items.en: The noun fault was applied to rock breaks, and line was the natural word for the trace where that break reaches the surface.
items.cn: 名词 fault 被用于岩石破裂，而 line 自然成为描述该破裂出露地表之迹线的词。

items.en: Survey geologists drew fault lines on maps, fixing the compound as a technical term.
items.cn: 地质调查人员在地图上画出断层线，使这个复合词固定为技术术语。

items.en: Journalists extended fault line to politics and society, where it names a division that can suddenly rupture.
items.cn: 记者把 fault line 扩展到政治与社会领域，用来指可能突然破裂的分裂线。

note.en: Group one holds compounds and single words that look or sound like fault line; group two holds nouns for rifts and divisions.
note.cn: 第一组是形音接近 fault line 的复合词与单词；第二组是表示裂痕与分裂的名词。

entries.definition: the break itself; fault line is only its surface trace or a metaphor built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 破裂本身；fault line 只是它在地表的迹线或由此构成的比喻。

entries.definition: defective; it is an adjective and has no line component.
entries.definitionCN: 有缺陷的；它是形容词，不含 line 成分。

entries.definition: the outer edge of a shape or a summary; it contains line but not fault.
entries.definitionCN: 形状的外缘或概要；它含 line 但不含 fault。

entries.definition: a reference line for measurement; the first element is base, not fault.
entries.definitionCN: 测量用的基准线；前半部分是 base，不是 fault。

entries.definition: a crack or a place where the crust is pulling apart; it is a widening gap, not a trace line.
entries.definitionCN: 裂缝，或地壳被拉开的地方；它是一条变宽的缝隙，不是迹线。

entries.definition: a long narrow crack in rock or ground; it describes the opening rather than the fault structure.
entries.definitionCN: 岩石或地面上细长的裂缝；它描述裂口本身，而非断层结构。

entries.definition: any break in a material; a fault line is a geological structure, while a fracture can be tiny.
entries.definitionCN: 材料中的任何断裂；断层线是地质构造，而断裂可以很小。

entries.definition: a separation between groups or regions; it lacks the image of sudden rupture.
entries.definitionCN: 群体或区域之间的分隔；它缺少「突然破裂」的形象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the compound is exactly its two parts, and the metaphor keeps the same geometry.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：这个复合词就是两个组成部分，而比喻也保持同样的几何关系。

normal.en: fault plus line: a fault is a surface, and its line is where that surface cuts the ground.
normal.cn: fault 加 line：断层是一个面，而这条线就是这个面切过地面的地方。

normal.en: A fault line on a map is drawn with a solid line where known and a dashed line where uncertain.
normal.cn: 地图上的断层线在确定处画实线，在不确定处画虚线。

normal.en: A political fault line works like a rock fault: two sides no longer line up, and stress can make them slip.
normal.cn: 政治上的 fault line 与岩石断层同理：两侧不再对齐，应力会让它们错动。

normal.en: A rift is an open gap; a fault line is the trace of the break that made it.
normal.cn: rift 是张开的缝隙；fault line 是造成这条缝的破裂迹线。

normal.en: The San Andreas Fault gives its name to a very well known fault line.
normal.cn: 圣安德烈斯断层给一条非常著名的断层线提供了名字。

abstract.en: Abstractly, a fault line is a place where a whole is already divided but still touching.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，fault line 是一个整体已经分开却仍然相接的地方。

abstract.en: The metaphor is useful because it predicts sudden change: quiet lines can rupture when stress accumulates.
abstract.cn: 这个比喻有用，因为它预示突然变化：平静的线在应力积累时会破裂。

abstract.en: Symbol: a thin broken line across a surface, with two blocks offset slightly on either side.
abstract.cn: 符号：地表一条细长的断续线，两侧岩块略微错开。

examples.en: The village lies directly on the fault line.
examples.cn: 这个村庄正好位于断层线上。

examples.en: Geologists traced the fault line for fifty kilometres.
examples.cn: 地质学家追踪这条断层线达五十公里。

examples.en: The election exposed a fault line inside the party.
examples.cn: 这次选举暴露出党内的一条分歧线。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「缝特 + 线」—— 岩层断开的缝在地面上连成一条线 → fault line 断层线

root: 由地质术语 fault（断层）与拉丁来源的 line（线）复合而成，字面义为「断层的线」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of fault line. The thread is a visible trace: first a rock break at the surface, then any line along which a whole may split.
sensesIntro.cn: fault line 的八个义项。主线是一条可见的迹线：先是地表出露的岩石破裂，再是任何可能使整体分裂的界线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a visible line where two blocks meet and no longer align.
core.cn: 核心意象：两块岩体相接却不再对齐的一条可见线。

branches.en: TRACE: the visible line and its drawn symbol on a map.
branches.cn: 迹线：可见的线，以及地图上的绘制符号。

branches.en: SEISMIC LINE: the line marks where earthquakes are expected.
branches.cn: 地震线：标出预期发生地震的位置。

branches.en: MATERIAL PATH: engineering borrows the image for a prepared line of failure.
branches.cn: 材料路径：工程借用这个形象指预设的破坏路径。

branches.en: SOCIAL RUPTURE: politics, society and organisations split along such a line.
branches.cn: 社会破裂：政治、社会与组织沿这样的线分裂。

branches.en: THE BROKEN BELT: the line stands for the shattered zone it runs through.
branches.cn: 破碎带：这条线代表它所穿过的破碎地带。

intro.en: Fault line is a compound of two complete words, so its analysis is the analysis of fault plus line.
intro.cn: fault line 是两个完整词构成的复合词，因此它的构词分析就是 fault 加 line 的分析。

latinIntro.en: Fault is from Latin fallere via Old French; line is from Latin linea 'string, line'. Both halves are Latin-derived, which is why latinEntries lists both.
latinIntro.cn: fault 经古法语来自拉丁语 fallere；line 来自拉丁语 linea「绳、线」。两半都源自拉丁语，因此 latinEntries 两侧都列。

items.example: The fault cuts through layered rock.
items.exampleCN: 这条断层切穿层状岩石。

items.meaning: a drawn stroke or a row of points
items.example: The line runs north to south.

items.meaning: the surface trace of a fault
items.example: The fault line passes under the town.

items.structure: fault line used as an adjective
items.meaning: relating to or along a fault line
items.meaningCN: 与断层线有关的，或沿断层线的
items.exampleCN: 断层线谷地沿破裂延伸。

items.meaning: the mapped path of the surface break
items.meaningCN: 地表破裂在地图上的路径
items.example: The fault-line trace is offset by a later quake.
items.exampleCN: 断层迹线被后来的地震错开。

items.meaning: the broken belt around the line
items.example: The fault zone is wider than the line itself.
items.exampleCN: 断层带比这条线本身更宽。

items.meaning: a large linear feature on the Earth's surface
items.example: Satellite images show a long lineament.
items.exampleCN: 卫星图像显示出一条长线状构造。

items.example: The boundary line follows the ridge.

definition_zh: 植物学；（某地区的）植物志
definition_en: the scientific study of plants, or the plant life of a particular region
core_image: 一张压制的叶片标本旁，摆着写满学名的标签与一把镊子
scene: 标本室里，学生把压制好的叶片按科属排进柜子，标签上写满学名。 Modern botany began when plants were classified by their parts rather than by their uses.
sceneCN: 这里 botany 指「植物学」（第 1 个义项：研究植物的科学）；句意为当植物按自身构造而非用途被分类时，现代植物学便开始了。

pos.zh: 植物学；植物区系；植物学著作

senses.title: The science of plants
senses.definition: the branch of biology that studies plants and their structure, growth and classification
senses.definitionCN: 研究植物及其结构、生长与分类的生物学分支
senses.example: Modern botany began with systematic classification.
senses.exampleCN: 现代植物学始于系统分类。
senses.why: the Greek root names herbage or fodder, so the science is literally the study of what grows as herb.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根指草料或饲草，因此这门科学字面上就是研究「长成草的东西」。

senses.title: The plant life of a region
senses.definition: all the plants growing in a particular area, considered as a group
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区生长的全部植物，作为整体来看
senses.example: The island's botany is dominated by ferns and mosses.
senses.exampleCN: 这个岛的植物以蕨与苔藓为主。
senses.why: a discipline can lend its name to its subject matter, as geology names the rocks of a region.
senses.whyCN: 学科名可以借给它的研究对象，正如地质学也用来说一个地区的岩石。

senses.title: The subject as taught
senses.definition: the school or university subject in which plants are studied
senses.definitionCN: 在学校或大学里研究植物的课程
senses.example: She took botany in her first year and never left the field.
senses.exampleCN: 她一年级修了植物学，从此没离开这个领域。
senses.why: the noun names the course because the course teaches the science, with no change of form.
senses.whyCN: 名词命名课程，因为课程所教的正是这门科学，词形没有变化。

senses.title: Economic botany
senses.titleCN: 经济植物学（把植物作为资源）
senses.definition: the study of plants as crops, medicines and raw materials
senses.definitionCN: 把植物作为作物、药材与原料来研究
senses.example: Economic botany traced the rubber plant from forest to factory.
senses.exampleCN: 经济植物学追溯橡胶植物从森林到工厂的路径。
senses.why: the field is defined by its use of plants, so an adjective narrows the general noun.
senses.whyCN: 这一领域以植物的用途来界定，因此用形容词收窄了通名。

senses.title: Field botany
senses.definition: the practical study of plants where they grow, chiefly by identifying them
senses.definitionCN: 在植物生长地进行的实务研究，主要是识别它们
senses.example: Field botany needs a hand lens and a great deal of patience.
senses.exampleCN: 野外植物学需要放大镜与极大的耐心。
senses.why: field marks the place of study, the opposite of laboratory botany.
senses.whyCN: 「野外」一词标记研究场所，与实验室植物学相对。

senses.title: Medical botany
senses.definition: the study of plants used as drugs or remedies
senses.definitionCN: 研究用作药物或疗法的植物
senses.example: Medical botany supplied most of the early pharmacopoeia.
senses.exampleCN: 早期的药典大多来自药用植物学。
senses.why: the adjective names the purpose, so the same science is practised for healing.
senses.whyCN: 形容词命名用途，同一门科学因此为治疗服务。

senses.title: A treatise or textbook of botany
senses.definition: a written work setting out the science of plants
senses.definitionCN: 系统阐述植物科学的著作
senses.example: He carried an old botany with him on every walk.
senses.exampleCN: 每次散步他都带着一本旧植物学书。
senses.why: a book is named after its subject, a common shorthand among sciences.
senses.whyCN: 书以主题命名，这是科学领域常见的简写。

senses.title: Systematic botany
senses.definition: the branch that names, describes and arranges plants into groups
senses.definitionCN: 命名、描述并把植物编入类群的分支
senses.example: Systematic botany still revises the family tree of flowering plants.
senses.exampleCN: 系统植物学仍在修订被子植物的谱系。
senses.why: systematic marks the classifying task, which is the oldest part of the science.
senses.whyCN: 「系统的」一词标记分类任务，而这门科学最古老的部分正是分类。

intro.en: Botany is the noun of botanic, from Latin botanicus and Greek botanikos 'of herbs', from botane 'grass, herb, fodder'. The deeper origin of botane is uncertain. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: botany 是 botanic 的名词，后者来自拉丁 botanicus 与希腊 botanikos「草本的」，出自 botane「草、草本、饲草」。botane 的更早来源不确定。年代均为约数。

items.en: Botane meant 'grass, herb, pasture, fodder'; the science therefore began as the study of herbage rather than of all plants.
items.cn: botane 意为「草、草本、牧场、饲草」；这门科学因此起初是研究草料，而非一切植物。

items.en: Botanikos 'of herbs' was the adjective used for knowledge about plants and their uses.
items.cn: botanikos「草本的」是用于指植物及其用途知识的形容词。

items.en: Latin took the Greek adjective as botanicus; the noun botanice followed in Medieval and Renaissance Latin.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊形容词借作 botanicus；名词 botanice 随后出现在中世纪与文艺复兴拉丁语中。

items.en: English botany is recorded in the seventeenth century, when plant study separated from medicine and agriculture.
items.cn: 英语 botany 于 17 世纪有记录，当时植物研究从医学与农业中分离出来。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Greek origin of botane is unresolved; its link to boskein 'to feed' is generally accepted within Greek but the deeper root is reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：botane 在希腊语之前的来源没有定论；它与 boskein「喂养」的联系在希腊语内部一般被接受，但更深的词根属重构。

items.en: Source uncertain (coining date): the exact first appearance of botany in English print is not settled, so the seventeenth-century dating is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（造词年代）：botany 首次见于英语印刷的确切时间尚无定论，因此 17 世纪的系年只是约数。

note.en: Group one separates the botanic family by part of speech; group two separates the science from its neighbouring disciplines and from plant cover.
note.cn: 第一组按词类区分 botanic 词族；第二组区分这门科学与相邻学科及植物覆盖。

entries.definition: Relating to plants or to botany; the adjective describes, while botany names the field.
entries.definitionCN: 与植物或植物学有关；形容词起描述作用，botany 命名领域。

entries.definition: A person who studies plants, formed with -ist; the field is botany, the practitioner is a botanist.
entries.definitionCN: 研究植物的人，由 -ist 构成；领域是 botany，从业者是 botanist。

entries.definition: To collect and study plants in the field; it is the verb, not the science.
entries.definitionCN: 在野外采集并研究植物；是动词，而非学科名。

entries.definition: The older adjective form, still used in names such as botanic garden; it is not a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 较老的形容词形式，仍见于「植物园」等名称；它不是名词。

entries.definition: The study of all living things; botany is the plant branch of it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究一切生物的科学；botany 是其中研究植物的分支。

entries.definition: The practice of growing garden plants; it applies botanical knowledge rather than producing it.
entries.definitionCN: 栽培园林植物的实务；它应用植物学知识，而非生产知识。

entries.definition: The plant species of a region or period, usually listed systematically; botany can also name the study of that list.
entries.definitionCN: 某地区或某时期的植物物种，通常系统列出；botany 也可指对这份名录的研究。

entries.definition: Plants as ground cover, described by structure rather than by species; it is what botany studies, not the study.
entries.definitionCN: 作为地面覆盖的植物，按结构而非物种描述；它是植物学的研究对象，而非这门学科。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek root, the real academic phrases and the real family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊词根、真实的学术搭配与真实词族。

normal.en: botane 'herb' + -y: the study of herbs, now of all plants.
normal.cn: botane「草本」+ -y：研究草本之学，如今研究一切植物。

normal.en: The family splits by word class: botany, botanic, botanical, botanist.
normal.cn: 词族按词类分开：botany、botanic、botanical、botanist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: field botany, economic botany, medical botany.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：野外植物学、经济植物学、药用植物学。

normal.en: The subject also names the plants of a place: the botany of an island.
normal.cn: 学科名也指一地植物：某岛的植物志。

normal.en: Its neighbour is zoology; together they were natural history.
normal.cn: 它的邻居是动物学；二者合起来曾是自然史。

abstract.en: Picture a pressed leaf beside a label written in careful Latin.
abstract.cn: 想象一片压制的叶子，旁边是工整拉丁文的标签。

abstract.en: Picture a walk that turns into a survey because every plant gets a name.
abstract.cn: 想象一次散步变成调查，因为每株植物都被取了名。

abstract.en: Picture a library where the shelves are organised by family rather than by use.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，书架按科属而非用途排列。

examples.en: Botany and zoology were once taught together as natural history.
examples.cn: 植物学与动物学曾作为自然史一起教授。

examples.en: The botany of the delta includes more than four hundred species.
examples.cn: 这片三角洲的植物超过四百种。

examples.en: Economic botany studies how plants become food, fibre and medicine.
examples.cn: 经济植物学研究植物如何变成食物、纤维与药物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「botan（草）+ y」——研究草与植物的学问 → 植物学

root: 希腊 botane「草、草本、饲草」→ botanikos「草本的」→ 拉丁 botanicus → 英语 botany。botane 的更早来源不确定，与 boskein「喂养」的联系在希腊语内部一般被接受。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of botany move from the science itself to the plants it studies, the course that teaches it, its applied branches and the book that records it.
sensesIntro.cn: botany 的八个义项从这门科学本身，移向它所研究的植物、教授它的课程、它的应用分支，以及记录它的书。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pressed leaf and a label written in Latin, side by side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片压制的叶子与一张拉丁文标签并排放着。

branches.en: SCIENCE AND SUBJECT MATTER: the discipline lends its name to the plants it studies.
branches.cn: 学科与对象：学科名借给它所研究的植物。

branches.en: TAUGHT AND WRITTEN: a course and a book both carry the name of the science.
branches.cn: 教与写：课程与书都以这门科学命名。

branches.en: APPLIED BRANCHES: crops and medicines narrow the field by purpose.
branches.cn: 应用分支：作物与药材按用途收窄领域。

branches.en: THE FIELD: identification outdoors is the oldest practical skill.
branches.cn: 野外：户外识别是最古老的实务技能。

branches.en: THE ORDER: naming and grouping is the backbone of the science.
branches.cn: 秩序：命名与归群是这门科学的骨干。

intro.en: Botany is a Greek adjective turned into an English noun, and its family names the field, the practitioner and the activity.
intro.cn: botany 是希腊形容词转成的英语名词，其词族命名领域、从业者与活动。

latinIntro.en: Greek botane 'herb' gives botanikos and Latin botanicus; English botany, botanic, botanical and botanist all descend from that adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 botane「草本」衍生 botanikos 与拉丁 botanicus；英语的 botany、botanic、botanical 与 botanist 都出自那个形容词。

items.example: The root names what grows as herb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名长成草的东西。

items.example: Botany names the study of plants.
items.exampleCN: botany 命名研究植物的学问。

items.example: The botanic garden holds living collections.

items.exampleCN: 植物学名遵循国际规则。

items.example: The botanist keyed out the unknown sedge.
items.exampleCN: 植物学家检索出了那种未知的莎草。

items.meaning: to collect plants in the field
items.example: They botanized the ridge before the road went in.
items.exampleCN: 在修路之前，他们在山脊采集植物。

items.meaning: the study of people's use of plants
items.example: Ethnobotany records which plants a village uses for medicine.
items.exampleCN: 民族植物学记录一个村庄用哪些植物做药。

items.example: Botanically, a tomato is a fruit.
items.exampleCN: 从植物学上看，番茄是果实。

definition_zh: 线粒体；真核细胞中进行有氧呼吸与能量转化的细胞器
definition_en: a membrane-bound organelle of eukaryotic cells that produces most of the cell's ATP by aerobic respiration and carries its own DNA
core_image: 一个椭圆形小囊，内膜反复向内折成层层皱褶，皱褶表面密布小颗粒，像塞满褶皱的暖手炉
scene: 这里指「线粒体」。 Each mitochondrion in the flight muscle is packed with cristae, because this tissue burns fuel faster than any other.
sceneCN: 这里 mitochondrion 指「线粒体」这一细胞器整体（第 1 个义项：具双层膜、能进行有氧呼吸并产生 ATP 的细胞器）；飞行肌里它数量极多，因为耗能最快。图中可辨识物件：双层膜、向内折的嵴、基质颗粒、椭圆形轮廓。

pos.zh: 线粒体（可数，复数 mitochondria，源自希腊中性 -on 变 -a）

derivatives.zh: 具线粒体的（原生生物学术语）

senses.title: The organelle itself
senses.definition: a double-membraned organelle of eukaryotic cells that carries out aerobic respiration
senses.definitionCN: 真核细胞中具双层膜、进行有氧呼吸的细胞器
senses.example: A muscle fibre may hold thousands of mitochondria.
senses.exampleCN: 一条肌纤维可容纳数千个线粒体。
senses.why: Greek mitos 'thread' and chondrion 'granule' were joined for a body seen as thread-like granules; the compound names the object, not its job.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 mitos「线」与 chondrion「小颗粒」被合成起来，指在染色下呈线状颗粒的小体；这个合成词命名的是对象，不是功能。

senses.title: Two membranes, folds and matrix
senses.titleCN: 线粒体的构造：双层膜、嵴、基质
senses.definition: the internal architecture of the organelle: an outer membrane, an inner membrane folded into cristae, and the matrix inside
senses.definitionCN: 该细胞器的内部构造：外膜、向内折成嵴的内膜，以及内部的基质
senses.example: The cristae multiply the inner surface where the electron transport chain sits.
senses.exampleCN: 嵴成倍扩大了电子传递链所在的内膜面积。
senses.why: the thread-granule image gains structure: the granule is a sac, and its inner skin is thrown into folds.
senses.whyCN: 「线状颗粒」这一意象获得了结构：颗粒是一个囊，其内皮被折成皱褶。

senses.title: The cell's aerobic power plant
senses.titleCN: 线粒体的功能：有氧呼吸与产能
senses.definition: the organelle's role as the main site of aerobic respiration and ATP production
senses.definitionCN: 该细胞器作为有氧呼吸与 ATP 生产主要场所的角色
senses.example: Without mitochondria the cell would rely on glycolysis alone.
senses.exampleCN: 没有线粒体，细胞就只能依靠糖酵解。
senses.why: the granule was soon found to consume oxygen and release energy, so its name came to stand for the cell's power supply.
senses.whyCN: 这种颗粒很快被发现消耗氧并释放能量，于是它的名字逐渐代指细胞的动力供应。

senses.title: The inner membrane as a battery
senses.titleCN: 内膜与电子传递：把质子梯度变成电
senses.definition: the inner membrane, where the electron transport chain builds a proton gradient that drives ATP synthase
senses.definitionCN: 内膜上电子传递链建立质子梯度、驱动 ATP 合酶的部位
senses.example: The inner mitochondrial membrane holds the pumps that acidify the intermembrane space.
senses.exampleCN: 线粒体内膜上装着把膜间隙变酸的质子泵。
senses.why: the folded skin is read as a device: its folds stack the machinery that turns electrons into a gradient.
senses.whyCN: 折起的皮被读成一台装置：皱褶把「把电子变成梯度」的机器叠放起来。

senses.title: The matrix where the cycle turns
senses.titleCN: 基质：三羧酸循环的场所
senses.definition: the gel inside the inner membrane, where the citric acid cycle and mitochondrial DNA reside
senses.definitionCN: 内膜内部的胶状物质，三羧酸循环与线粒体 DNA 所在之处
senses.example: Enzymes of the citric acid cycle float in the mitochondrial matrix.
senses.exampleCN: 三羧酸循环的酶漂浮在线粒体基质中。
senses.why: the inside of the granule is given its own contents, so the organelle is also a chamber with a chemical address.
senses.whyCN: 颗粒内部被赋予了自己的内容物，于是这个细胞器也是一个带化学「地址」的腔室。

senses.title: Its own DNA and maternal line
senses.titleCN: 自有 DNA 与母系遗传
senses.definition: the small circular genome inside the organelle, inherited through the mother in most animals
senses.definitionCN: 细胞器内部的小型环状基因组，在多数动物中经母系传递
senses.example: Mitochondrial DNA mutates fast and is passed only through the egg.
senses.exampleCN: 线粒体 DNA 突变较快，且只经由卵细胞传递。
senses.why: the granule turned out to carry its own instructions, so it is read as a semi-independent tenant rather than a pure tool.
senses.whyCN: 这种颗粒被发现自带指令，于是被读成半独立的住客，而不是纯粹的工具。

senses.title: Fission, fusion and a moving network
senses.definition: the organelle as a population that constantly divides and fuses, forming a network rather than fixed beads
senses.definitionCN: 该细胞器作为不断分裂与融合的群体，形成网络而非固定的珠粒
senses.example: Live imaging shows mitochondria fusing and splitting within seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 活细胞成像显示线粒体在数秒内融合与分裂。
senses.why: once filmed alive, the separate granules prove to be one shifting net, so the noun also names a dynamic system.
senses.whyCN: 活体拍摄后，看似分离的颗粒显现为一张流动的网，因此这个名词也命名一个动态系统。

senses.title: Gatekeeper of programmed death
senses.definition: the organelle's role in releasing signals that commit a cell to programmed death
senses.definitionCN: 该细胞器释放信号、决定细胞进入程序性死亡的角色
senses.example: Cytochrome release from mitochondria triggers the death cascade.
senses.exampleCN: 线粒体释放细胞色素 c 会触发死亡级联。
senses.why: because it holds the energy and the signals, the organelle is read as a switch between living on and shutting down.
senses.whyCN: 因为它同时掌握能量与信号，这个细胞器被读成「继续活」与「关机」之间的开关。

intro.en: Mitochondrion is a nineteenth-century scientific compound from Greek mitos 'thread' and chondrion, a diminutive of chondros 'grain, cartilage'. It is not a classical Latin word.
intro.cn: mitochondrion 是 19 世纪的科学合成词，来自希腊语 mitos「线」与 chondrion（chondros「颗粒、软骨」的指小形式）。它不是古典拉丁词。

items.en: Greek mitos named a warp thread and, by extension, anything thread-like. The older pre-Greek origin of the word is not established.
items.cn: 希腊语 mitos 指织机的经线，引申指任何线状物。该词在希腊语之前的更早来源并无定论。

items.en: chondros meant 'grain' and also 'cartilage'; its diminutive chondrion named a small granule. Both senses are classical.
items.cn: chondros 意为「颗粒」，也指「软骨」；其指小形式 chondrion 指小颗粒。两个义项均为古典用法。

items.en: Carl Benda coined mitochondrium in 1898 for granules seen in stained cells. The plural mitochondria follows the Greek neuter pattern -on to -a.
items.cn: Carl Benda 于 1898 年为染色细胞中见到的颗粒创造了 mitochondrium；复数 mitochondria 遵循希腊中性名词 -on 变 -a 的规则。

items.en: Source uncertain: joining mitos to chondrion is generally explained as describing thread-like granules in muscle preparations, but Benda's own stated reason is not documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定：把 mitos 与 chondrion 组合起来，一般解释为描述肌肉标本中的线状颗粒，但 Benda 本人陈述的理由并无文献记录。

items.en: English took the word in the early twentieth century through German cytology; the first English citation is approximate.
items.cn: 英语于 20 世纪初经德国细胞学传入；最早的英语书证年代为约数。

items.en: New Latin mitochondrium is only a Latinized spelling of the Greek compound; it is not an inherited Latin word, so no classical Latin root should be claimed for it.
items.cn: 新拉丁语 mitochondrium 只是这个希腊合成词的拉丁化拼写，并非传承的拉丁词，因此不应为它主张古典拉丁词根。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes built from the same Greek pieces but naming different things; group two holds other cell structures often confused with it.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊构词成分、却指不同事物的形近词；第二组是易与之混淆的其他细胞结构。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of or in a mitochondrion'. It cannot stand alone for the organelle itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为「线粒体的、线粒体内的」，不能单独指这个细胞器本身。

entries.definition: Shares Greek mitos 'thread' because of the thread-like chromosomes, but names cell division, not an organelle.
entries.definitionCN: 同出希腊 mitos「线」，因染色体呈线状而得名，但指细胞分裂，不是细胞器。

entries.definition: Built on chondros 'cartilage' plus kytos 'cell'; it names a cartilage cell and has nothing to do with energy production.
entries.definitionCN: 由 chondros「软骨」加 kytos「细胞」构成，指软骨细胞，与产能无关。

entries.definition: From mitos 'thread' (via mitosis) plus -gen 'producer': a substance that triggers cell division, not a granule.
entries.definitionCN: 由 mitos「线」经 mitosis 加 -gen「产生者」构成：触发细胞分裂的物质，不是颗粒。

entries.definition: Any specialised compartment of a cell. A mitochondrion is one member of that class.
entries.definitionCN: 指细胞内任何特化的区室；线粒体是这一类中的一个成员。

entries.definition: The plastid that runs photosynthesis. It also has its own DNA, but it captures energy instead of releasing it from fuel.
entries.definitionCN: 进行光合作用的质体；它同样有自身 DNA，但它捕获能量，而不是从燃料中释放能量。

entries.definition: The plant-cell family of double-membraned organelles to which chloroplasts belong; mitochondria are a separate lineage.
entries.definitionCN: 植物细胞中具双层膜的细胞器家族，叶绿体属于其中；线粒体是另一支系。

entries.definition: One inward fold of the inner membrane. Cristae are parts of a mitochondrion, not the organelle.
entries.definitionCN: 指内膜的一道向内皱褶；嵴是线粒体的一部分，而不是细胞器本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: mitos 'thread' + chondrion 'granule': thread-like granules, the literal name Benda gave the organelle.
normal.cn: mitos「线」+ chondrion「颗粒」：线状颗粒，这正是 Benda 给该细胞器的字面命名。

normal.en: The family runs mitochondrion, mitochondria, mitochondrial, mitochondrially.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mitochondrion、mitochondria、mitochondrial、mitochondrially。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the parts: outer membrane, inner membrane, cristae, matrix, mitochondrial DNA.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各部分：外膜、内膜、嵴、基质、线粒体 DNA。

normal.en: Biology checks the numbers: prokaryote 70S versus eukaryote 80S ribosomes, and hundreds of mitochondria per liver cell.
normal.cn: 生物学用数字核对：原核 70S 与真核 80S 核糖体，以及每个肝细胞数百个线粒体。

normal.en: The plural -a is the Greek neuter rule, the same one behind phenomenon and phenomena.
normal.cn: 复数 -a 是希腊中性规则，与 phenomenon 变 phenomena 同一条。

abstract.en: Picture a small stove inside a room, its flues folded again and again to give off more heat.
abstract.cn: 想象房间里的小炉子，烟道反复折回以放出更多热。

abstract.en: Picture a bean-shaped sack whose inner lining is crumpled like paper packed into a jar.
abstract.cn: 想象一个豆形囊，内衬被揉皱得像塞进罐子的纸。

abstract.en: Picture a tenant who keeps a copy of the house key and can lock the door from inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一个租客自己留着一把钥匙，能从里面把门锁上。

examples.en: Sperm cells carry mitochondria in the midpiece to power the tail.
examples.cn: 精子在中段携带线粒体，为尾部提供能量。

examples.en: A mutation in mitochondrial DNA can impair hearing and muscle control.
examples.cn: 线粒体 DNA 的突变可损害听力与肌肉控制。

examples.en: The cristae of heart mitochondria are denser than those of skin cells.
examples.cn: 心肌线粒体的嵴比皮肤细胞的更密。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买（mito）一个会喘气的小颗粒（chondrion）」——细胞里不停烧燃料产能的颗粒 → 线粒体

root: 希腊 mitos「线」+ chondrion「小颗粒」（chondros「颗粒、软骨」的指小形式）→ 新拉丁 mitochondrium（1898）→ 英语 mitochondrion；复数 mitochondria。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a thread-like granule is opened up, and that opening is read as a sac, a fold, a power plant, a battery, a chamber, a tenant with its own DNA, a moving net, and finally a death switch.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：「线状颗粒」被拆开，而这一拆开依次被读成囊、皱褶、发电厂、电池、腔室、自带 DNA 的住客、流动的网，最后是生死开关。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small granule whose inner skin is folded into a stack of plates.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗小颗粒，内皮被折成一叠板。

branches.en: THE OBJECT NAMED: the compound starts as a label for a visible body in stained cells.
branches.cn: 被命名的对象：这个合成词起初只是染色细胞中一个可见小体的标签。

branches.en: ARCHITECTURE: the granule is resolved into two membranes, folds and a matrix.
branches.cn: 构造：颗粒被解析成两层膜、皱褶与基质。

branches.en: ENERGY: the folded lining is a power plant, and its folds are the battery plates.
branches.cn: 能量：折起的内衬是发电厂，皱褶就是电池极板。

branches.en: CONTENTS: the inner chamber holds a chemical cycle and a private genome.
branches.cn: 内容物：内腔装着一条化学循环与一份私有的基因组。

branches.en: LIFE AND DEATH: the population fuses and divides, and can also issue the order to die.
branches.cn: 生与死：这一群体既融合分裂，也能发出死亡的指令。

intro.en: Mitochondrion is a Greek compound behind a Latinized ending; the pieces are two bound combining forms, not a prefix plus root.
intro.cn: mitochondrion 是拉丁化词尾包裹的希腊合成词；其构件是两个粘着组合形式，而不是前缀加词根。

latinIntro.en: There is no inherited Latin source. New Latin mitochondrium merely re-spells the Greek compound, and mitochondrial is the English adjective built with Latin -alis.
latinIntro.cn: 没有传承的拉丁来源。新拉丁语 mitochondrium 只是把这个希腊合成词改写为拉丁拼法，mitochondrial 则是用拉丁 -alis 构成的英语形容词。

items.example: One mitochondrion was followed for ten minutes under the microscope.
items.exampleCN: 在显微镜下对单个线粒体追踪了十分钟。

items.example: The cell's mitochondria form a connected network.
items.exampleCN: 细胞的线粒体构成一个连通网络。

items.example: Mitochondrial proteins are imported from the cytoplasm.
items.exampleCN: 线粒体蛋白由细胞质输入。

items.example: Amitochondriate protists lack the organelle entirely.
items.exampleCN: 无线粒体的原生生物完全没有这一细胞器。
线粒体生成需要两套基因组。

items.example: The child was diagnosed with a mitochondriopathy.
items.exampleCN: 该儿童被诊断出线粒体病。

items.meaning: the small genome inside the organelle
items.meaningCN: 线粒体内的环状基因组
items.example: Mitochondrial DNA is inherited from the mother.
items.exampleCN: 线粒体 DNA 由母方遗传。

definition_zh: 磨损；消耗；人员自然减员；逐步削弱
definition_en: a gradual wearing down or reduction, whether of material, people or strength
core_image: 两块石头在水流里互相摩擦，棱角一年年变小，最后只剩光滑的卵石
scene: 项目组没有裁员，只是不再补缺，两年后办公室里少了三分之一的人。 The company managed the decline by attrition rather than layoffs.
sceneCN: 这里 attrition 指靠不补缺实现的人员自然减员（第 2 个义项：自然减员）；句意为公司靠自然减员而不是裁员来应对规模缩减。

pos.zh: 磨损；消耗；自然减员；逐步削弱

senses.title: Wearing away by friction
senses.definition: the gradual wearing away of a surface by continuous rubbing
senses.definitionCN: 表面因持续摩擦而逐渐损耗
senses.example: The tyres showed heavy attrition after two seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 两个赛季之后，轮胎磨损严重。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to rub against'; the noun names what rubbing leaves behind, a surface slowly losing its material.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「相互摩擦」；名词命名摩擦留下的结果，即表面慢慢失去材质。

senses.title: Natural staff reduction
senses.definition: a decrease in staff numbers achieved by not replacing those who leave
senses.definitionCN: 不补替离职者，从而实现员工人数下降
senses.example: The firm reduced its payroll through attrition.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司靠自然减员来缩减人员开支。
senses.why: People leave for their own reasons; if no one replaces them, the group shrinks without a single dismissal, which is a quiet form of wearing down.
senses.whyCN: 人们因自己的原因离开；若不补人，团队就在没有一次解雇的情况下缩小，这是一种安静的消耗。

senses.title: Gradual weakening
senses.definition: a slow loss of strength, morale or numbers under sustained pressure
senses.definitionCN: 在持续压力下力量、士气或人数的缓慢流失
senses.example: The long campaign caused serious attrition in the ranks.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的战役让队伍严重损耗。
senses.why: Morale is also a material: every small setback takes a little away, and no single defeat is responsible for the total.
senses.whyCN: 士气也是一种材料：每次小挫折都带走一点，总量不由任何一次失败单独负责。

senses.title: A war of attrition
senses.definition: a conflict in which each side tries to exhaust the other rather than win a decisive battle
senses.definitionCN: 各方试图耗尽对方而非争取决定性胜利的冲突
senses.example: The border dispute became a war of attrition.
senses.exampleCN: 这场边境争端变成了一场消耗战。
senses.why: When neither side can strike a finish, the aim shifts from beating the enemy to making the enemy spend more than it can replace.
senses.whyCN: 当双方都无法一击定局时，目标就从打败敌人转为让敌人消耗超过其补充能力。

senses.title: Loss of members or customers
senses.definition: the gradual loss of members, customers or students over time
senses.definitionCN: 成员、客户或学生随时间逐渐流失
senses.example: The gym's attrition rate worried its owners.
senses.exampleCN: 这家健身房的会员流失率让老板担忧。
senses.why: Members leave one at a time for ordinary reasons; the total loss is visible only in the rate.
senses.whyCN: 成员因日常原因一个一个离开；总损失只能从流失率上看见。

senses.title: Rock erosion
senses.definition: the grinding down of rock fragments by water, wind or ice
senses.definitionCN: 岩石碎片被水、风或冰磨小
senses.example: River pebbles are shaped by decades of attrition.
senses.exampleCN: 河里的卵石是数十年磨蚀塑成的。
senses.why: Water carries sand that acts as grit, so the stone is rubbed by the load it travels with.
senses.whyCN: 水流携带沙砾作为磨料，于是石头被同行的负载磨小。

senses.title: Theological attrition
senses.titleCN: 神学意义上的「下等痛悔」
senses.definition: in theology, sorrow for sin caused by fear of punishment rather than by love of God
senses.definitionCN: 在神学中，因害怕惩罚而非因爱上帝产生的悔罪
senses.example: The old manual distinguishes attrition from contrition.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的手册把下等痛悔与上等痛悔区分开来。
senses.why: Theological writing borrowed the wear image: fear rubs the will down without changing its love.
senses.whyCN: 神学写作借用了磨损意象：恐惧磨低意志，却不改变它的爱。

senses.title: Wear from sustained use
senses.definition: the slow decline of equipment or material through ordinary use
senses.definitionCN: 设备或材料因日常使用而缓慢退化
senses.example: The museum limited handling because of attrition to the binding.
senses.exampleCN: 由于装帧不断损耗，博物馆限制了翻阅。
senses.why: Every use removes a little material; the noun measures that total loss rather than any single break.
senses.whyCN: 每次使用都带走一点材料；这个名词衡量的是总损失，而不是某一次断裂。

intro.en: Attrition comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to rub against', the same root family as trite and detritus.
intro.cn: attrition 来自一个意为「相互摩擦」的拉丁动词，与 trite、detritus 同属一个词根家族。

items.en: English took the noun in the 15c. for rubbing or friction, and later used it for staff loss and for exhausting wars.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个名词，表示摩擦；后来用于人员流失与消耗战。

items.en: Attritio meant 'a rubbing against, friction, wear', the noun of action from atterere.
items.cn: attritio 意为「摩擦、磨损」，是 atterere 的动作名词。

items.en: Atterere 'to rub against, wear down' is ad- 'to' plus terere 'to rub'.
items.cn: atterere「摩擦、磨掉」由 ad-「向」与 terere「摩擦」构成。

items.en: Terere 'to rub' also gives trite, originally 'rubbed smooth', and detritus, the material rubbed away.
items.cn: terere「摩擦」也产生 trite（原意「被磨平」）与 detritus（被磨掉的碎屑）。

items.en: The idea of material rubbed away became the idea of people or strength quietly drained, especially in business and military writing.
items.cn: 材料被磨掉的概念，变成人员或力量被悄然耗尽的概念，在商业与军事文本中尤其常见。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the rubbing root; the near-meaning group names ways of being worn down or drained.
note.cn: 形近组共享「摩擦」词根；近义组列出被磨耗或耗尽的各种方式。

entries.definition: relating to wearing down or gradual loss.
entries.definitionCN: 与磨损或逐步流失有关。

entries.definition: to wear down or reduce gradually.
entries.definitionCN: 逐步磨损或削减。

entries.definition: deep sorrow for wrongdoing, from the same Latin terere.
entries.definitionCN: 对过错的深切悔恨，来自同一拉丁词 terere。

entries.definition: debris worn away from a larger mass.
entries.definitionCN: 从大块物质上磨掉的碎屑。

entries.definition: the gradual wearing away of rock or soil.
entries.definitionCN: 岩石或土壤逐渐被磨去。

entries.definition: damage caused by continuous use or friction.
entries.definitionCN: 持续使用或摩擦造成的损伤。

entries.definition: the reduction of a resource until little remains.
entries.definitionCN: 资源被消耗到所剩无几。

entries.definition: loss of employees, students or materials that could have been used.
entries.definitionCN: 本可利用的员工、学生或材料的损失。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of two stones grinding each other smaller.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「两块石头互相磨小」的画面留住。

normal.en: Think of tri, to rub: attrition is the result of steady rubbing.
normal.cn: 想想词根 terere「摩擦」：attrition 就是持续摩擦的结果。

normal.en: Picture two river stones knocking together until the corners are gone.
normal.cn: 想象两块河石不断相撞，直到棱角消失。

normal.en: A company that does not replace leavers is worn down the same way.
normal.cn: 不补替离职者的公司，也是以同样的方式被磨小。

normal.en: In a war of attrition, the goal is not to win but to outlast.
normal.cn: 在消耗战中，目标不是取胜，而是撑得比对方久。

normal.en: Say at-TRI-tion, with the rubbing root stressed in the middle.
normal.cn: 读成 at-TRI-tion，重音落在表示「摩擦」的词根上。

abstract.en: No single blow explains the loss; the total comes from repetition.
abstract.cn: 没有哪一次打击能解释全部损失；总量来自重复。

abstract.en: People are a resource that can be drained quietly, without a dismissal.
abstract.cn: 人是一种可以被安静耗尽的资源，不必经过解雇。

abstract.en: What remains after attrition is smooth, smaller and easier to overlook.
abstract.cn: 磨耗之后剩下的东西更光滑、更小，也更容易被忽视。

examples.en: The tyres showed heavy attrition after two seasons.
examples.cn: 两个赛季之后，轮胎磨损严重。

examples.en: The firm reduced its payroll through attrition.
examples.cn: 这家公司靠自然减员来缩减人员开支。

examples.en: The border dispute became a war of attrition.
examples.cn: 这场边境争端变成了一场消耗战。

dict_mnemonic.text: at（向）+ trit（摩擦）+ ion（名词）：不断相互摩擦，就是「磨损、消耗」。

root: 拉丁语 attritio（摩擦），源自 atterere：ad-（向）+ terere（摩擦）

sensesIntro.en: Attrition is always loss by repetition rather than by one blow; the senses differ in whether the material lost is stone, rubber, staff, morale or customers.
sensesIntro.cn: attrition 始终是「重复造成的损失」而非一次打击；各义项的差别在于失去的材料是石头、橡胶、员工、士气还是客户。

core.en: LOSS BY STEADY RUBBING
core.cn: 持续摩擦造成的损失

branches.en: Stone, rubber and surfaces worn by friction.
branches.cn: 被摩擦磨损的石头、橡胶与表面。

branches.en: People and members lost by not replacing them.
branches.cn: 因不补替而流失的员工与成员。

branches.en: The general decline of strength or morale.
branches.cn: 力量或士气的普遍下滑。

branches.en: The strategy that aims to exhaust rather than defeat.
branches.cn: 旨在耗尽而非击败的战略。

branches.en: The old theological sense, and loss through ordinary use.
branches.cn: 古老的神学义，以及日常使用造成的损耗。

intro.en: The word is a Latin noun of action on a verb meaning to rub, with English relatives that keep the same image.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「摩擦」动词的动作名词，其英语同族词保留同一意象。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show rubbing becoming friction, then wear, then quiet depletion.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁语条目展示「摩擦」如何变成「磨损」，再变成「悄然耗尽」。

items.exampleCN: 人员损耗已经削减了团队。

items.example: The enemy was attrited by raids.

items.meaning: a grinding down of the spirit

items.example: Creation is the act of creating.

definition_zh: 拱顶；穹窿；地下室；金库；墓室；跳跃；撑杆跳
definition_en: an arched ceiling or a room covered by one, a secure underground room, or a leap over something
core_image: 弧形石顶从两侧墙脚上升，在正中交会；地面之下另有一间锁着的石室，走廊尽头则有人撑杆跃过横杆
scene: 教堂中殿上方的石顶由两侧墙脚起弧，在正中交会。 The vault above the nave has carried the roof for eight centuries.
sceneCN: 这里 vault 指「覆盖空间的拱形顶棚」（第 1 个义项：拱顶、穹窿）；句意为中殿上方的拱顶已承住屋顶八个世纪。图中可辨识物件：弧形石顶、两侧墙脚、中殿、屋顶。

pos.zh: 拱顶；穹窿；地下室；金库；墓室
跳跃越过；撑杆跳

senses.title: An arched ceiling
senses.definition: a ceiling formed by an arch or a series of arches
senses.definitionCN: 由一道拱或一系列拱构成的顶棚
senses.example: The barrel vault runs the whole length of the corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 筒形拱顶贯通整条走廊。
senses.why: the word came from a Latin term for something rolled or turned, and an arch turned over a space is exactly that shape.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语中表示「卷、转」的说法，而绕空间翻转的拱正是那种形状。

senses.title: The space under a vault
senses.definition: a room or passage roofed by an arch
senses.definitionCN: 由拱顶覆盖的房间或通道
senses.example: The vault under the choir is open to visitors in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 唱诗席下方的拱顶空间夏季向访客开放。
senses.why: a roof and the room it covers are so closely joined that one word names both.
senses.whyCN: 屋顶与其覆盖的房间结合得太紧，于是一个词兼指两者。

senses.title: An underground storage room
senses.definition: a secure room below ground, often bricked or stone-lined
senses.definitionCN: 地下安全房间，常以砖石砌成
senses.example: The wine vault stays at a constant twelve degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 酒窖常年保持十二度。
senses.why: stone-lined cellars were built with arched roofs, so the roof word became the room word.
senses.whyCN: 石砌地窖多用拱形顶，因此屋顶词变成房间词。

senses.title: A bank's strong room
senses.definition: a heavily protected room where money and valuables are kept
senses.definitionCN: 存放金钱与贵重物品的强力防护房间
senses.example: The bank vault opens only with two separate keys.
senses.exampleCN: 银行金库只有用两把不同的钥匙才能打开。
senses.why: security borrowed the cellar's solidity, and the word now suggests steel and locks rather than stone.
senses.whyCN: 保安借用了地窖的坚固感，这个词如今让人想到钢与锁，而非石头。

senses.title: A family burial chamber
senses.definition: a stone room beneath a church or in a cemetery used for burials
senses.definitionCN: 教堂之下或墓地中用于安葬的石室
senses.example: Three generations are buried in the vault under the chapel.
senses.exampleCN: 有三代人葬在小教堂下的墓室里。
senses.why: the underground arched room was a natural place for the dead, so the word acquired a funerary sense.
senses.whyCN: 地下的拱形房间很适合安置死者，因此这个词获得了丧葬义。

senses.title: A crypt beneath a church
senses.definition: the vaulted chamber under the main altar of a church
senses.definitionCN: 教堂主祭坛下的拱顶房间
senses.example: The crypt vault was dug in the eleventh century.
senses.exampleCN: 这座地下墓室建于十一世纪。
senses.why: church building gave the underground room a precise liturgical place and name.
senses.whyCN: 教堂建筑赋予地下房间一个精确的礼仪位置与名称。

senses.title: A leap over an obstacle
senses.definition: a jump made with the hands or a pole, especially over something
senses.definitionCN: 用手或杆完成的跳跃，尤指越过某物
senses.example: He cleared the fence with a single vault.
senses.exampleCN: 他一跃就越过了围栏。
senses.why: this sense came through a different French verb meaning to turn or tumble, and a turning body is a leaping body.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项来自另一个法语动词，意为翻转或翻滚，而翻转的身体正是跳跃的身体。

senses.title: The pole vault event
senses.definition: the athletics event in which an athlete clears a bar with a long pole
senses.definitionCN: 运动员用长杆越过横杆的田径项目
senses.example: She set the national record in the vault last season.
senses.exampleCN: 上个赛季她在撑杆跳项目上刷新了全国纪录。
senses.why: the event name is the leap noun narrowed into a sport with rules and a bar.
senses.whyCN: 项目名是把跳跃名词收窄为有规则与横杆的运动。

intro.en: Vault is two senses from one Latin rolling root: a turned roof and a turned body. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: vault 的两个义项同出一个拉丁语「滚动」词根：翻转的屋顶与翻转的身体。年代均为约数。

items.en: Volvere meant to roll, turn or wrap around, and it supplied a family of words about curved and rolling motion.
items.cn: volvere 意为滚动、转动或缠绕，衍生出一族关于曲线与滚动运动的词。

items.en: Voluta named a spiral or scroll shape, and it described the curled capital of a column.
items.cn: voluta 指螺旋或涡卷形状，也描述柱头的卷曲。

items.en: A later form named a turn or an arched covering, and Old French voute carried the roof sense to English.
items.cn: 后期形式指转弯或拱形覆盖，古法语 voute 把屋顶义带入英语。

items.en: A related verb meant to turn or tumble, and its English descendant gave the leap sense.
items.cn: 一个相关动词意为翻转或翻滚，其英语后裔给出了跳跃义。

items.en: Romanesque and Gothic masons made the vault a structural system, and the word followed stone, cellar and tomb.
items.cn: 罗曼式与哥特式石匠把拱顶发展成结构体系，这个词随石头、地窖与墓室延伸。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin ancestry of volvere is not settled, and the Indo-European root commonly proposed for it is a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深来源）：volvere 在拉丁语之前的谱系尚无定论，通常为其提出的印欧语词根是重构形式，而非有记录的形式。

note.en: Group one holds curved-roof words and easily confused forms; group two holds secure rooms and jumping words.
note.cn: 第一组是曲面屋顶词与易混形式；第二组是安全房间与跳跃词。

entries.definition: Having a vault; it describes a building rather than naming the roof.
entries.definitionCN: 有拱顶的；描述建筑，而非命名屋顶。

entries.definition: A spiral scroll on an Ionic capital, from the same Latin rolling root.
entries.definitionCN: 爱奥尼柱头上的螺旋涡卷，同出拉丁「滚动」词根。

entries.definition: The unit of electrical force, named after an Italian scientist; it has no connection to the roof word.
entries.definitionCN: 电动势单位，以意大利科学家命名，与屋顶词无关。

entries.definition: It can mean either the building of vaults or the act of leaping; context decides which.
entries.definitionCN: 既指建造拱顶，也指跳跃动作，由语境决定。

entries.definition: A rounded roof over a circular space; a vault is usually arched along a line or a grid.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖圆形空间的圆顶；拱顶通常沿一条线或网格起拱。

entries.definition: A stone chamber beneath a church, usually for burial; it often has a vault but need not.
entries.definitionCN: 教堂下的石室，通常用于安葬；常有拱顶，但非必需。

entries.definition: An underground storage room, usually for wine or goods; it is plainer than the secure vault.
entries.definitionCN: 地下储藏室，通常存酒或货物；比强调安全性的 vault 朴素。

entries.definition: A jump, often a long one; vault is a leap over an obstacle or with a pole.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指跳跃，常指远跳；vault 是越过障碍或以杆完成的跳。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real rolling root, the real building terms and the real athletics event.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「滚动」词根、真实的建筑术语与真实的田径项目。

normal.en: One root means roll or turn: a turned roof and a turning body gave the two main senses.
normal.cn: 同一个词根意为滚动或转动：翻转的屋顶与翻转的身体给出两个主要义项。

normal.en: The family runs vault, vaulted, vaulting, vaulter, pole vault, vault-like.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 vault、vaulted、vaulting、vaulter、pole vault、vault-like。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: barrel vault, ribbed vault, bank vault, burial vault, pole vault.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各分支：筒形拱顶、肋拱顶、银行金库、家族墓室、撑杆跳。

normal.en: A stone roof over a cellar became the word for the cellar and then for a bank's strong room.
normal.cn: 地窖上的石顶先成为地窖之名，再成为银行金库之名。

normal.en: The gymnastics sense keeps the turning body, not the stone.
normal.cn: 跳跃义保留的是翻转的身体，而非石头。

abstract.en: Picture a stone bowl turned upside down and buried halfway.
abstract.cn: 想象一只石碗倒扣过来，一半埋进土里。

abstract.en: Picture a locked room under a church where the only light comes from the door.
abstract.cn: 想象教堂之下一间上锁的屋子，唯一的光来自门口。

abstract.en: Picture a body turning in the air as if rolling over an invisible line.
abstract.cn: 想象一具身体在空中翻转，仿佛越过一条看不见的线。

examples.en: The vault of the nave is held by ribs of cut stone.
examples.cn: 中殿的拱顶由切石肋支撑。

examples.en: The documents were moved to a vault during the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水期间，文件被转移到金库。

examples.en: He vaulted the low wall without breaking stride.
examples.cn: 他一步未停就越过了矮墙。

dict_mnemonic.text: volvere（滚动、翻转）→ 翻转成拱的顶 → 拱顶、地下室、金库；翻转身体 → 跳跃

root: 拉丁 volvere「滚动、翻转」衍生 voluta「涡卷」与后期 volta「拱形覆盖」，经古法语 voute 入英语；跳跃义经古法语 volter「翻转、翻滚」而来。英语 vault。volvere 的更早来源不确定，相关印欧词根属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one turn: a roof turns over a space, the room beneath it becomes a cellar, a strong room and a tomb, while a turning body becomes a leap and a sport.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次翻转展开：屋顶绕空间翻转，其下的房间成为地窖、金库与墓室；而翻转的身体成为跳跃与运动项目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curve rising from two feet and meeting at the middle, and a body turning over a bar.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条从两侧墙脚升起、在中间交会的曲线，以及一具越过横杆翻转的身体。

branches.en: THE ROOF: the first sense is the curved ceiling itself.
branches.cn: 屋顶：第一个义项就是曲面顶棚本身。

branches.en: THE ROOM BELOW: a vaulted space and a storage cellar are the roof and the room it shelters.
branches.cn: 其下的房间：拱顶空间与储藏地窖，是屋顶与它所庇护的房间。

branches.en: SECURE DEPTHS: a bank's strong room, a family tomb and a church crypt all turn the underground room into protection.
branches.cn: 安全的地下：银行金库、家族墓室与教堂地下墓室，都把地下房间变成保护。

branches.en: THE TURNED BODY: the leap comes from the same root's idea of turning over.
branches.cn: 翻转的身体：跳跃来自同一词根「翻转」的观念。

branches.en: THE SPORT: the leap is narrowed into an event with a pole and a bar.
branches.cn: 运动：跳跃被收窄为有杆与横杆的项目。

intro.en: Vault comes from a Latin rolling verb, so its affix list follows one root through roof, room and leap.
intro.cn: vault 来自一个拉丁语「滚动」动词，因此其词缀清单沿同一词根贯穿屋顶、房间与跳跃。

latinIntro.en: Latin volvere and voluta stand behind the roof sense, while the leap sense came through a French verb for turning over.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 volvere 与 voluta 支撑屋顶义，而跳跃义经一个表示翻转的法语动词而来。

items.structure: volvere, volvi, volutum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The root pictures motion around a centre.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根描绘绕中心的运动。

items.example: A voluta curls at the top of a column.

items.meaning: an arched ceiling; a secure room

items.exampleCN: 有拱顶的地窖保持凉爽。

items.meaning: vault construction, or the act of leaping
items.example: Vaulting began with stone and ended in sport.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从石头开始，最后落到运动。

items.example: The vaulter cleared the bar on the third try.
items.exampleCN: 撑杆跳选手第三次越过横杆。

items.meaning: the athletics event of jumping with a pole
items.example: The pole vault needs speed and timing.
items.exampleCN: 撑杆跳需要速度与时机。
